- `harness-runtime` and `harness-engine` are both empty stub crates (doc comment only) — Phase 2 is fully greenfield.

- **Dependency bugs found:** Task 2.4 (`FakeBackend`) and Task 2.5 (`FakeToolExecutor`) list only Phase‑1 dependencies, but both implement traits that don't exist until Task 2.6. //! Core runtime traits for execution backends and tool executors.
//!
//! This module defines the two primary async traits that the harness runtime
//! uses to drive model/agent execution ([`ExecutionBackend`]) and tool I/O
//! ([`ToolExecutor`]), together with supporting type aliases and the
//! [`ToolRegistry`] struct.
//!
//! Both traits are designed to be *dyn*-compatible via [`async_trait`],
//! enabling heterogeneous registries (e.g. `HashMap<ToolId, Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>`)
//! and per-session backend injection (`Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>`).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_protocol::backend::{
    BackendCapabilities, BackendDescriptor, ExecutionContext, ExecutionError, ExecutionEvent,
    ExecutionRequest, ExecutionResult,

/// An unbounded channel sender through which backends stream

///

/// every event it produces (text deltas, reasoning deltas, tool call requests,
/// usage updates, completion, errors).  The channel is unbounded so the
/// backend never blocks on event emission — backpressure is handled at a
/// higher level (e.g. via the scheduler or per-agent budgets).
pub type ExecutionEventSink = tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<ExecutionEvent>;

/// An unbounded channel sender through which tool executors stream
/// [`ToolProgress`] updates to the agent runner.
///
/// The executor calls [`send`](tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender::send) for
/// each progress update (e.g. "reading file…", "50% complete").  Like
/// [`ExecutionEventSink`], this channel is unbounded to avoid backpressure
/// during tool execution.
pub type ToolEventSink = tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<ToolProgress>;

// Tool execution context

/// execution, such as workspace access, environment variables, and
/// per-execution metadata.  The exact set of fields will grow as more
/// tool types are integrated (e.g. filesystem tools need a workspace
/// handle, shell tools need working-directory information).
///

/// - `env: HashMap<String, String>` — environment variables.

    /// Reserved for future use.  Currently a zero-sized placeholder
    /// that allows the type to exist without forcing every tool

    pub _private: (),
}

    /// without internal knowledge of the struct's fields.  New fields
    /// will be added via builder-pattern methods or additional

    }
}

        Self::new()
    }

/// An execution backend capable of running model/agent inference.
///
/// This is the primary abstraction for normalising different execution
/// systems — raw model APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), higher-level
/// agent integrations (Claude Code, Codex), and test doubles — behind a
/// single interface.
///
/// ## Contract
///
/// 1. [`descriptor`](ExecutionBackend::descriptor) and
///    [`capabilities`](ExecutionBackend::capabilities) are infallible,
///    cheap, and must not perform I/O.
///
/// 2. [`execute`](ExecutionBackend::execute) is the only entry point for
///    running a request.  It **must**:
///    - Stream events through `events` as they become available (text
///      deltas, reasoning deltas, tool calls, usage updates).
///    - Respect the `cancel` token — if cancelled it should stop producing
///      events and return [`ExecutionError::Cancelled`] (or cease event
///      emission and allow the caller to detect cancellation).
///    - Return [`ExecutionResult`] on success or [`ExecutionError`] on
///      failure.
///
/// 3. Implementations **must not** branch on agent identity — the caller
///    uses [`capabilities`](ExecutionBackend::capabilities) for
///    feature-detection.
///
/// ## Dyn compatibility
///
/// This trait is decorated with [`#[async_trait]`](async_trait) and
/// requires `Send + Sync`, which allows it to be stored as
/// `Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>` and shared across tasks.

    /// capabilities).

    /// should return a fixed descriptor rather than constructing one on
    /// every call.

    ///
    /// This is a convenience accessor equivalent to
    /// `self.descriptor().capabilities` but without the overhead of
    /// cloning the full descriptor every time a caller only needs the
    /// capabilities.
    fn capabilities(&self) -> BackendCapabilities;

    ///
    /// # Parameters
    ///
    /// * `request` — The full request payload including system prompt,
    ///   message history, and available tools.
    /// * `context` — Execution parameters (max tokens, temperature, stop
    ///   sequences).
    /// * `events` — An unbounded sender for streaming execution events.
    ///   The backend **must** send all events through this channel and
    ///   close it (drop the sender) when execution finishes.
    /// * `cancel` — A cancellation token.  The backend **should** poll
    ///   this token and abort execution when cancelled.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    ///
    /// `Ok(ExecutionResult)` on success, `Err(ExecutionError)` on failure.
    ///
    /// # Cancellation
    ///
    /// When the `cancel` token is triggered, the backend **should**:
    /// - Stop producing new events.
    /// - Drop the `events` sender.
    /// - Return `Err(ExecutionError::Cancelled)`.
    ///
    /// However, the caller **must not** rely on the return value to detect
    /// cancellation — the caller should also poll the cancellation token
    /// independently.
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        request: ExecutionRequest,
        context: ExecutionContext,
        events: ExecutionEventSink,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError>;
}

// ToolExecutor trait
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A concrete executor for a single tool.
///
/// Each tool in the system has a corresponding `ToolExecutor` registered
/// in the [`ToolRegistry`].  The executor is responsible for performing
/// the tool's actual I/O — reading files, executing shell commands,
/// searching the workspace, etc. — and streaming progress events back
/// to the agent runner.
///
/// ## Contract
///
/// 1. [`descriptor`](ToolExecutor::descriptor) is infallible, cheap, and
///    must not perform I/O.  It returns the [`ToolDescriptor`] that
///    describes this tool's identity, schema, and human-readable metadata.
///
/// 2. [`execute`](ToolExecutor::execute) performs the tool action:
///    - It receives the deserialised `arguments` as a
///      [`serde_json::Value`] (the caller validates the shape against
///      `descriptor().input_schema`).
///    - It streams [`ToolProgress`] updates through `events`.
///    - It respects the `cancel` token.
///    - It returns [`ToolResult`] on success or [`ToolError`] on failure.
///
/// ## Dyn compatibility
///
/// Like [`ExecutionBackend`], this trait is `#[async_trait]` + `Send + Sync`
/// so it can be stored as `Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>` in the registry.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolExecutor: Send + Sync {
    /// Returns the descriptor for this tool.
    ///
    /// The descriptor is used by the runtime to advertise available tools
    /// to the agent and to validate tool-call arguments against the input
    /// schema.
    fn descriptor(&self) -> ToolDescriptor;

    /// Execute this tool with the given arguments.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    ///
    /// * `context` — Execution context (currently a placeholder, will
    ///   carry workspace handles, environment, etc.).
    /// * `arguments` — The deserialised arguments for this invocation.
    ///   The shape must match `descriptor().input_schema`.
    /// * `events` — An unbounded sender for streaming progress updates.
    /// * `cancel` — A cancellation token.  The executor **should** abort
    ///   execution when the token is cancelled.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    ///
    /// `Ok(ToolResult)` with the tool's output on success,
    /// `Err(ToolError)` on failure.
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        context: ToolExecutionContext,
        arguments: serde_json::Value,
        events: ToolEventSink,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ToolResult, ToolError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolRegistry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A registry of all tool executors known to the runtime.
///
/// The registry is a simple map from [`ToolId`] to an [`Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>`].
/// Tools are registered once at startup (typically by the application or
/// extension system) and then looked up by the agent runner when the model
/// requests a tool call.
///
/// # Agent-level filtering
///
/// The registry holds **all** executors the runtime knows about.  A
/// specific agent may only see a subset of these — the agent's
/// [`AgentToolset`](harness_protocol::tools::AgentToolset) controls which
/// tools are visible and what permission policy applies.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ToolRegistry {
    /// Maps tool IDs to their corresponding executors.
    executors: HashMap<ToolId, Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>,
}

impl ToolRegistry {
    /// Create an empty tool registry.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            executors: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Register a tool executor, keyed by its [`ToolId`].
    ///
    /// If a tool with the same `id` was already registered, the old
    /// executor is replaced and returned.
    pub fn register(&mut self, executor: Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>) -> Option<Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>> {
        let id = executor.descriptor().id;
        self.executors.insert(id, executor)
    }

    /// Look up a tool executor by [`ToolId`].
    ///
    /// Returns `None` if no executor is registered for the given `id`.
    pub fn get(&self, id: &ToolId) -> Option<&Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>> {
        self.executors.get(id)
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over all registered (tool-id, executor) pairs.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&ToolId, &Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>)> {
        self.executors.iter()
    }

    /// Returns the number of registered executors.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.executors.len()
    }

    /// Returns `true` if no executors are registered.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.executors.is_empty()
    }

    /// Returns a list of descriptors for all registered tools.
    ///
    /// This is useful for building a [`ToolDescriptor`] list to advertise
    /// to a backend (after filtering through an agent's [`AgentToolset`]).
    pub fn descriptors(&self) -> Vec<ToolDescriptor> {
        self.executors
            .values()
            .map(|executor| executor.descriptor())
            .collect()
    }
}

impl FromIterator<Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>> for ToolRegistry {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>>(iter: I) -> Self {
        let mut registry = ToolRegistry::new();
        for executor in iter {
            registry.register(executor);
        }
        registry
    }
}

//!
//! This module defines the two primary async traits that the harness runtime
//! uses to drive model/agent execution ([`ExecutionBackend`]) and tool I/O
//! ([`ToolExecutor`]), together with supporting type aliases and the
//! [`ToolRegistry`] struct.
//!
//! Both traits are designed to be *dyn*-compatible via [`async_trait`],
//! enabling heterogeneous registries (e.g. `HashMap<ToolId, Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>`)
//! and per-session backend injection (`Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>`).

/// The backend calls [`send`](tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender::send) for
/// every event it produces (text deltas, reasoning deltas, tool call requests,

/// backend never blocks on event emission — backpressure is handled at a
/// higher level (e.g. via the scheduler or per-agent budgets).

/// [`ToolProgress`] updates to the agent runner.

/// The executor calls [`send`](tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender::send) for
/// each progress update (e.g. "reading file…", "50% complete").  Like
/// [`ExecutionEventSink`], this channel is unbounded to avoid backpressure
/// during tool execution.

/// An execution backend capable of running model/agent inference.

/// ## Contract
///
/// 1. [`descriptor`](ExecutionBackend::descriptor) and

///    cheap, and must not perform I/O.

/// 2. [`execute`](ExecutionBackend::execute) is the only entry point for
///    running a request.  It **must**:

///    - Respect the `cancel` token — if cancelled it should stop producing
///      events and return [`ExecutionError::Cancelled`] (or cease event
///      emission and allow the caller to detect cancellation).
///    - Return [`ExecutionResult`] on success or [`ExecutionError`] on
///      failure.

///

/// requires `Send + Sync`, which allows it to be stored as

    ///

/// A scripted outcome for a single tool invocation.
///
/// Used with [`FakeToolExecutor`] to specify what a given tool call should
/// return when [`execute`](FakeToolExecutor::execute) is invoked.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum FakeToolOutcome {
    /// The executor returns `Ok(result)`, producing a successful tool
    /// response with the given [`ToolResult`].
    Ok(ToolResult),

    /// The executor returns `Err(error)`, signalling a tool-level failure.
    Err(ToolError),
}

impl FakeToolOutcome {
    /// Shorthand for a successful (non-error) result.
    ///
    /// Equivalent to `FakeToolOutcome::Ok(ToolResult { call_id, output, is_error: false })`.
    pub fn ok(call_id: ToolCallId, output: serde_json::Value) -> Self {
        Self::Ok(ToolResult {
            call_id,
            output,
            is_error: false,
        })
    }

    /// Shorthand for a logical error result (the tool ran but indicates a
    /// problem in its output, such as "file not found").
    ///
    /// Equivalent to `FakeToolOutcome::Ok(ToolResult { call_id, output, is_error: true })`.
    pub fn error_result(call_id: ToolCallId, output: serde_json::Value) -> Self {
        Self::Ok(ToolResult {
            call_id,
            output,
            is_error: true,
        })
    }

    /// Shorthand for an executor-level failure.
    ///
    /// Equivalent to `FakeToolOutcome::Err(error)`.
    pub fn err(error: ToolError) -> Self {
        Self::Err(error)
    }
}

// FakeToolExecutor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A fake [`ToolExecutor`] that returns pre-scripted outcomes in sequence.
///
/// Each call to [`execute`](FakeToolExecutor::execute) consumes the next
/// outcome from the script queue.  When the script is exhausted the
/// executor returns `Err(ToolError::Internal)`.
///
/// The executor is `Send + Sync` and can be stored as
/// `Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>` for use in [`ToolRegistry`](crate::traits::ToolRegistry)
/// and agent-runner tests.
///
/// # Determinism
///
/// Outcomes are consumed in strict FIFO order — the first call to
/// `execute` returns the first scripted outcome, the second call returns
/// the second, and so on.  This makes tests fully deterministic as long
/// as the number of expected tool invocations matches the script length.
///
/// # Cancellation
///
/// If the [`CancellationToken`] is cancelled before the outcome is
/// popped, the executor returns `Err(ToolError::Timeout)` immediately.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```ignore
/// use harness_protocol::ids::ToolCallId;
/// use harness_protocol::tools::{ToolDescriptor, ToolError, ToolResult};
/// use harness_runtime::testing::fake_tools::{FakeToolExecutor, FakeToolOutcome};
/// use harness_runtime::traits::ToolExecutionContext;
/// use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;
/// use tokio::sync::mpsc;
///
/// let descriptor = ToolDescriptor {
///     id: ToolId::new(),
///     name: "test_tool".into(),
///     description: "A fake tool for testing".into(),
///     input_schema: serde_json::json!({}),
/// };
///
/// let call_id = ToolCallId::new();
/// let outcomes = vec![
///     FakeToolOutcome::ok(call_id, serde_json::json!({"result": "success"})),
///     FakeToolOutcome::err(ToolError::ExecutionFailed),
/// ];
///
/// let executor = FakeToolExecutor::new(descriptor, outcomes);
/// let (_tx, rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
/// let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
/// let context = ToolExecutionContext::new();
///
/// // First call → Ok
/// let result = executor.execute(context.clone(), serde_json::json!({}), rx.clone(), cancel.clone()).await;
/// assert!(result.is_ok());
///
/// // Second call → Err(ExecutionFailed)
/// let result = executor.execute(context, serde_json::json!({}), rx, cancel).await;
/// assert!(result.is_err());
/// ```
pub struct FakeToolExecutor {
    /// The static descriptor returned by [`descriptor()`](Self::descriptor).
    descriptor: ToolDescriptor,
    /// The queue of remaining scripted outcomes, protected by a mutex for
    /// interior mutability (required because `execute` takes `&self`).
    outcomes: Mutex<VecDeque<FakeToolOutcome>>,
}

impl FakeToolExecutor {
    /// Creates a new executor with the given `descriptor` and scripted
    /// `outcomes`.
    ///
    /// The outcomes are consumed in FIFO order — the first call to
    /// [`execute`](Self::execute) returns the first outcome, the second
    /// call returns the second, and so on.
    pub fn new(descriptor: ToolDescriptor, outcomes: Vec<FakeToolOutcome>) -> Self {
        Self {
            descriptor,
            outcomes: Mutex::new(VecDeque::from(outcomes)),
        }
    }

    /// Creates a new executor with the given `descriptor` and an empty
    /// script.
    ///
    /// Every call to [`execute`](Self::execute) will return
    /// `Err(ToolError::Internal)` until outcomes are added via
    /// [`push_outcome`](Self::push_outcome).
    pub fn with_descriptor(descriptor: ToolDescriptor) -> Self {
        Self {
            descriptor,
            outcomes: Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Appends an outcome to the end of the script queue.
    ///
    /// This can be called at any time — even after some outcomes have
    /// already been consumed — to extend the script dynamically.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if the internal mutex is poisoned (a panic occurred while
    /// the lock was held in another thread).
    pub fn push_outcome(&self, outcome: FakeToolOutcome) {
        self.outcomes
            .lock()
            .expect("FakeToolExecutor outcome lock poisoned")
            .push_back(outcome);
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolExecutor for FakeToolExecutor {
    fn descriptor(&self) -> ToolDescriptor {
        self.descriptor.clone()
    }

    async fn execute(
        &self,
        _context: ToolExecutionContext,
        _arguments: serde_json::Value,
        events: ToolEventSink,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ToolResult, ToolError> {
        // Honour cancellation — check at the entry point before
        // accessing any internal state.
        if cancel.is_cancelled() {
            let _ = events.send(ToolProgress {
                status: "cancelled".into(),
                fraction: 1.0,
            });
            return Err(ToolError::Timeout);
        }

        // Pop the next scripted outcome from the front of the queue.
        let outcome = {
            let mut guard = self
                .outcomes
                .lock()
                .expect("FakeToolExecutor outcome lock poisoned");
            guard.pop_front()
        };

        match outcome {
            None => {
                // Script exhausted — no outcome remains to return.
                let _ = events.send(ToolProgress {
                    status: "internal error — no scripted outcome available".into(),
                    fraction: 1.0,
                });
                Err(ToolError::Internal)
            }
            Some(FakeToolOutcome::Ok(result)) => {
                let _ = events.send(ToolProgress {
                    status: "completed".into(),
                    fraction: 1.0,
                });
                Ok(result)
            }
            Some(FakeToolOutcome::Err(error)) => {
                let _ = events.send(ToolProgress {
                    status: "error".into(),
                    fraction: 1.0,
                });
                Err(error)
            }
        }
    }
}

//! [`AgentCommand`]s from its mailbox, applying them to the agent's
//! deterministic state machine, and dispatching the resulting
//! [`AgentEffect`]s.
//!
//! ## Architecture
//!
//! ```text
//!                     ┌──────────────────┐
//!   mpsc::Receiver ◄──│   AgentCommand   │
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!                              ▼

//!                              │

//!               ▼              ▼              ▼

//! ```

use tokio::sync::{broadcast, mpsc};
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_protocol::commands::{AgentCommand, AgentResult};
use harness_protocol::effects::AgentEffect;
use harness_protocol::events::{AgentEventEnvelope, EventVisibility};
use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, EventId, Timestamp};

/// Mailbox and lifecycle primitives for driving a single agent.
///
/// This struct bundles the communication channels needed to send commands
/// to an agent, receive its events, and cancel its execution.
///
/// # Channel semantics
///
/// * **`commands`** (`mpsc::Receiver`) — the inbound command stream.  The
///   runner reads from this channel in a loop.  When the sender half is
///   dropped, the channel yields `None`, which causes the runner to exit.
///
/// * **`events`** (`broadcast::Sender`) — the outbound event bus.  Every
///   [`AgentEventEnvelope`] produced by the agent is published here.
///   Multiple subscribers (session bus, UI, logging) can independently
///   consume the stream.
///
/// * **`cancel`** (`CancellationToken`) — cooperative shutdown signal.
///   When triggered while the runner is waiting for a command, the runner
///   exits its event loop immediately.
pub struct AgentTask {
    /// The agent this task is associated with.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// Incoming command channel — the runner reads from this receiver.
    pub commands: mpsc::Receiver<AgentCommand>,
    /// Outgoing event channel — the runner publishes [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s
    /// on this sender so downstream consumers (session bus, UI, etc.) can
    /// observe agent activity.
    pub events: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    /// Cooperative cancellation token. When cancelled, the runner exits its
    /// event loop.
    pub cancel: CancellationToken,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Runtime executor that drives a single agent through its lifecycle.
///
/// The runner owns both the agent's deterministic core ([`Agent`]) and its
/// communication channels ([`AgentTask`]).  It runs an async event loop:
///
/// 1. Wait for the next [`AgentCommand`] from the mailbox (or a cancellation
///    signal).
/// 2. Apply the command to the agent via [`Agent::apply`] — a pure,
///    synchronous transition that mutates the agent's state and returns a
///    list of [`AgentEffect`]s.
/// 3. Interpret each effect:
///    * [`AgentEffect::Emit`] — wraps the inner [`AgentEvent`] in an
///      [`AgentEventEnvelope`] (filling in session/agent/sequence metadata)
///      and forwards it on the broadcast channel.
///    * [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`] — records the [`AgentResult`] so
///      callers can inspect it later (no external trait object required).
///    * All other effects — `ExecuteBackend`, `ExecuteTool`, `SpawnAgent`,
///      `RequestPermission`, `CancelBackend`, `CancelTool`, `CancelChild`,
///      `Persist` — require external trait objects or runtime coordination
///      and are **not** handled in this base implementation.
///
/// # State after completion
///
/// After a run finishes (success, failure, or cancellation), the agent
/// transitions to `Idle` or `Failed` and remains available to accept new
/// commands.  The runner therefore continues its event loop until the
/// command channel is closed or cancellation is requested.
pub struct AgentRunner {
    /// The agent's deterministic state machine.
    agent: Agent,
    /// The mailbox and lifecycle primitives.
    task: AgentTask,
    /// Monotonic counter scoped to this agent, used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of
    /// every emitted envelope.
    agent_sequence: u64,
    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    last_result: Option<AgentResult>,
}

impl AgentRunner {
    /// Create a new runner that owns the given `agent` and `task`.
    pub fn new(agent: Agent, task: AgentTask) -> Self {
        Self {
            agent,
            task,
            agent_sequence: 0,
            last_result: None,
        }
    }

    /// Run the event loop until the command channel closes or the
    /// cancellation token is triggered.
    ///
    /// After this method returns the caller can use
    /// [`into_agent`](Self::into_agent) to retrieve the agent (with its
    /// final state) or inspect [`last_result`](Self::last_result).
    pub async fn run(&mut self) {
        loop {
            tokio::select! {
                biased; // check cancellation first when both are ready

                _ = self.task.cancel.cancelled() => {
                    break;
                }

                cmd = self.task.commands.recv() => {
                    let Some(cmd) = cmd else {
                        // The sender was dropped; no more commands will arrive.
                        break;
                    };
                    self.handle_command(cmd).await;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Command → effect pipeline
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Apply a single command to the agent and dispatch every returned effect.
    async fn handle_command(&mut self, command: AgentCommand) {
        let effects = self.agent.apply(command);
        for effect in effects {
            self.handle_effect(effect).await;
        }
    }

    /// Interpret a single effect returned by the agent core.
    async fn handle_effect(&mut self, effect: AgentEffect) {
        match effect {
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Emit — wrap in an envelope and broadcast to subscribers
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::Emit { event } => {
                let envelope = AgentEventEnvelope {
                    event_id: EventId::new(),
                    session_id: self.agent.session_id,
                    agent_id: self.agent.id,
                    parent_agent_id: self.agent.parent_id,
                    run_id: self.agent.state.active_run,
                    agent_sequence: self.agent_sequence,
                    session_sequence: None, // assigned by session bus later
                    timestamp: Timestamp::now(),
                    visibility: EventVisibility::User,
                    event,
                };
                self.agent_sequence += 1;

                // `send` returns an error only when there are no active
                // receivers — that is a normal condition (e.g., no UI is
                // subscribed), so we silently ignore it.
                let _ = self.task.events.send(envelope);
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // FinishRun — store the result; the agent is still alive
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::FinishRun { result } => {
                self.last_result = Some(result);
                // The run is finished, but the agent can still accept new
                // commands (StartRun, Cancel, etc.).
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Unhandled effects — require external coordination
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            //
            // The following effects all require some form of external trait
            // object (e.g., an ExecutionBackend, ToolExecutor, PermissionUI,
            // SessionStore) that is outside the scope of this base loop.
            //
            // Downstream runners should extend or override handle_effect to
            // provide the necessary dispatch for these variants.
            AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend { .. }
            | AgentEffect::ExecuteTool { .. }
            | AgentEffect::SpawnAgent { .. }
            | AgentEffect::RequestPermission { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelBackend { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelTool { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelChild { .. }
            | AgentEffect::Persist { .. } => {
                // Intentionally a no-op in the base implementation.
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Accessors
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Shared reference to the inner agent (e.g. for inspecting state).
    pub fn agent(&self) -> &Agent {
        &self.agent
    }

    /// Mutable reference to the inner agent (e.g. for pre-populating state
    /// before the loop starts).
    pub fn agent_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Agent {
        &mut self.agent
    }

    /// Consume the runner and return the owned agent with its final state.
    pub fn into_agent(self) -> Agent {
        self.agent
    }

    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    ///
    /// This is set each time the agent emits an [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`]
    /// effect, which happens at the end of every run (success, failure, or
    /// cancellation).
    pub fn last_result(&self) -> Option<&AgentResult> {
        self.last_result.as_ref()
    }

    /// The current monotonic agent-sequence counter.
    ///
    /// This is the value that will be used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of the
    /// *next* emitted envelope.
    pub fn agent_sequence(&self) -> u64 {
        self.agent_sequence
    }
}

    /// [`AgentEventEnvelope`] on the broadcast channel with correct
    /// session and agent metadata.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn emit_effect_forwards_event() {
        let (cmd_tx, cmd_rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(16);
        let (evt_tx, mut evt_rx) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel(64);
        let cancel = tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken::new();

        let agent_id = runner.agent().id;

        cmd_tx
            .send(AgentCommand::StartRun {

                    text: "hello".into(),
                    attachments: vec![],

            .await
            .expect("send StartRun");

        drop(cmd_tx);

        let envelope = evt_rx.try_recv().expect("should have received an event");
        assert_eq!(envelope.agent_id, agent_id);

//! Core runtime traits for execution backends and tool executors.
//!
//! This module defines the two primary async traits that the harness runtime
//! uses to drive model/agent execution ([`ExecutionBackend`]) and tool I/O
//! ([`ToolExecutor`]), together with supporting type aliases and the
//! [`ToolRegistry`] struct.
//!
//! Both traits are designed to be *dyn*-compatible via [`async_trait`],
//! enabling heterogeneous registries (e.g. `HashMap<ToolId, Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>`)
//! and per-session backend injection (`Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>`).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_protocol::backend::{
    BackendCapabilities, BackendDescriptor, ExecutionContext, ExecutionError, ExecutionEvent,
    ExecutionRequest, ExecutionResult,
};
use harness_protocol::ids::ToolId;
use harness_protocol::tools::{ToolDescriptor, ToolError, ToolProgress, ToolResult};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Event sinks
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// An unbounded channel sender through which backends stream
/// [`ExecutionEvent`]s to the agent runner.
///
/// The backend calls [`send`](tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender::send) for
/// every event it produces (text deltas, reasoning deltas, tool call requests,
/// usage updates, completion, errors).  The channel is unbounded so the
/// backend never blocks on event emission — backpressure is handled at a
/// higher level (e.g. via the scheduler or per-agent budgets).
pub type ExecutionEventSink = tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<ExecutionEvent>;

/// An unbounded channel sender through which tool executors stream
/// [`ToolProgress`] updates to the agent runner.
///
/// The executor calls [`send`](tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender::send) for
/// each progress update (e.g. "reading file…", "50% complete").  Like
/// [`ExecutionEventSink`], this channel is unbounded to avoid backpressure
/// during tool execution.
pub type ToolEventSink = tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<ToolProgress>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tool execution context
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Context provided to a tool executor when a tool is invoked.
///
/// This struct carries runtime dependencies that a tool may need during
/// execution, such as workspace access, environment variables, and
/// per-execution metadata.  The exact set of fields will grow as more
/// tool types are integrated (e.g. filesystem tools need a workspace
/// handle, shell tools need working-directory information).
///
/// # Future expansion
///
/// Planned fields include:
/// - `workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>` — for filesystem tool access.
/// - `env: HashMap<String, String>` — environment variables.
/// - `working_dir: PathBuf` — the directory the tool should run in.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ToolExecutionContext {
    /// Reserved for future use.  Currently a zero-sized placeholder
    /// that allows the type to exist without forcing every tool
    /// implementation to depend on workspace or environment types that
    /// have not yet been stabilised.
    pub _private: (),
}

impl ToolExecutionContext {
    /// Creates a new, empty tool execution context.
    ///
    /// This constructor exists so that callers can produce a context
    /// without internal knowledge of the struct's fields.  New fields
    /// will be added via builder-pattern methods or additional
    /// constructors as the runtime evolves.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { _private: () }
    }
}

impl Default for ToolExecutionContext {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ExecutionBackend trait
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// An execution backend capable of running model/agent inference.
///
/// This is the primary abstraction for normalising different execution
/// systems — raw model APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), higher-level
/// agent integrations (Claude Code, Codex), and test doubles — behind a
/// single interface.
///
/// ## Contract
///
/// 1. [`descriptor`](ExecutionBackend::descriptor) and
///    [`capabilities`](ExecutionBackend::capabilities) are infallible,
///    cheap, and must not perform I/O.
///
/// 2. [`execute`](ExecutionBackend::execute) is the only entry point for
///    running a request.  It **must**:
///    - Stream events through `events` as they become available (text
///      deltas, reasoning deltas, tool calls, usage updates).
///    - Respect the `cancel` token — if cancelled it should stop producing
///      events and return [`ExecutionError::Cancelled`] (or cease event
///      emission and allow the caller to detect cancellation).
///    - Return [`ExecutionResult`] on success or [`ExecutionError`] on
///      failure.
///
/// 3. Implementations **must not** branch on agent identity — the caller
///    uses [`capabilities`](ExecutionBackend::capabilities) for
///    feature-detection.
///
/// ## Dyn compatibility
///
/// This trait is decorated with [`#[async_trait]`](async_trait) and
/// requires `Send + Sync`, which allows it to be stored as
/// `Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>` and shared across tasks.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ExecutionBackend: Send + Sync {
    /// Returns the backend's descriptor (id, name, description,
    /// capabilities).
    ///
    /// This is a cheap, synchronous, infallible accessor.  Implementations
    /// should return a fixed descriptor rather than constructing one on
    /// every call.
    fn descriptor(&self) -> BackendDescriptor;

    /// Returns the backend's capability flags.
    ///
    /// This is a convenience accessor equivalent to
    /// `self.descriptor().capabilities` but without the overhead of
    /// cloning the full descriptor every time a caller only needs the
    /// capabilities.
    fn capabilities(&self) -> BackendCapabilities;

    /// Execute a request against this backend.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    ///
    /// * `request` — The full request payload including system prompt,
    ///   message history, and available tools.
    /// * `context` — Execution parameters (max tokens, temperature, stop
    ///   sequences).
    /// * `events` — An unbounded sender for streaming execution events.
    ///   The backend **must** send all events through this channel and
    ///   close it (drop the sender) when execution finishes.
    /// * `cancel` — A cancellation token.  The backend **should** poll
    ///   this token and abort execution when cancelled.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    ///
    /// `Ok(ExecutionResult)` on success, `Err(ExecutionError)` on failure.
    ///
    /// # Cancellation
    ///
    /// When the `cancel` token is triggered, the backend **should**:
    /// - Stop producing new events.
    /// - Drop the `events` sender.
    /// - Return `Err(ExecutionError::Cancelled)`.
    ///
    /// However, the caller **must not** rely on the return value to detect
    /// cancellation — the caller should also poll the cancellation token
    /// independently.
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        request: ExecutionRequest,
        context: ExecutionContext,
        events: ExecutionEventSink,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolExecutor trait
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A concrete executor for a single tool.
///
/// Each tool in the system has a corresponding `ToolExecutor` registered
/// in the [`ToolRegistry`].  The executor is responsible for performing
/// the tool's actual I/O — reading files, executing shell commands,
/// searching the workspace, etc. — and streaming progress events back
/// to the agent runner.
///
/// ## Contract
///
/// 1. [`descriptor`](ToolExecutor::descriptor) is infallible, cheap, and
///    must not perform I/O.  It returns the [`ToolDescriptor`] that
///    describes this tool's identity, schema, and human-readable metadata.
///
/// 2. [`execute`](ToolExecutor::execute) performs the tool action:
///    - It receives the deserialised `arguments` as a
///      [`serde_json::Value`] (the caller validates the shape against
///      `descriptor().input_schema`).
///    - It streams [`ToolProgress`] updates through `events`.
///    - It respects the `cancel` token.
///    - It returns [`ToolResult`] on success or [`ToolError`] on failure.
///
/// ## Dyn compatibility
///
/// Like [`ExecutionBackend`], this trait is `#[async_trait]` + `Send + Sync`
/// so it can be stored as `Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>` in the registry.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolExecutor: Send + Sync {
    /// Returns the descriptor for this tool.
    ///
    /// The descriptor is used by the runtime to advertise available tools
    /// to the agent and to validate tool-call arguments against the input
    /// schema.
    fn descriptor(&self) -> ToolDescriptor;

    /// Execute this tool with the given arguments.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    ///
    /// * `context` — Execution context (currently a placeholder, will
    ///   carry workspace handles, environment, etc.).
    /// * `arguments` — The deserialised arguments for this invocation.
    ///   The shape must match `descriptor().input_schema`.
    /// * `events` — An unbounded sender for streaming progress updates.
    /// * `cancel` — A cancellation token.  The executor **should** abort
    ///   execution when the token is cancelled.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    ///
    /// `Ok(ToolResult)` with the tool's output on success,
    /// `Err(ToolError)` on failure.
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        context: ToolExecutionContext,
        arguments: serde_json::Value,
        events: ToolEventSink,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ToolResult, ToolError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolRegistry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A registry of all tool executors known to the runtime.
///
/// The registry is a simple map from [`ToolId`] to an [`Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>`].
/// Tools are registered once at startup (typically by the application or
/// extension system) and then looked up by the agent runner when the model
/// requests a tool call.
///
/// # Agent-level filtering
///
/// The registry holds **all** executors the runtime knows about.  A
/// specific agent may only see a subset of these — the agent's
/// [`AgentToolset`](harness_protocol::tools::AgentToolset) controls which
/// tools are visible and what permission policy applies.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ToolRegistry {
    /// Maps tool IDs to their corresponding executors.
    executors: HashMap<ToolId, Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>,
}

impl ToolRegistry {
    /// Create an empty tool registry.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            executors: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Register a tool executor, keyed by its [`ToolId`].
    ///
    /// If a tool with the same `id` was already registered, the old
    /// executor is replaced and returned.
    pub fn register(&mut self, executor: Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>) -> Option<Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>> {
        let id = executor.descriptor().id;
        self.executors.insert(id, executor)
    }

    /// Look up a tool executor by [`ToolId`].
    ///
    /// Returns `None` if no executor is registered for the given `id`.
    pub fn get(&self, id: &ToolId) -> Option<&Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>> {
        self.executors.get(id)
    }

    /// Returns an iterator over all registered (tool-id, executor) pairs.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&ToolId, &Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>)> {
        self.executors.iter()
    }

    /// Returns the number of registered executors.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.executors.len()
    }

    /// Returns `true` if no executors are registered.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.executors.is_empty()
    }

    /// Returns a list of descriptors for all registered tools.
    ///
    /// This is useful for building a [`ToolDescriptor`] list to advertise
    /// to a backend (after filtering through an agent's [`AgentToolset`]).
    pub fn descriptors(&self) -> Vec<ToolDescriptor> {
        self.executors
            .values()
            .map(|executor| executor.descriptor())
            .collect()
    }
}

impl FromIterator<Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>> for ToolRegistry {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>>(iter: I) -> Self {
        let mut registry = ToolRegistry::new();
        for executor in iter {
            registry.register(executor);
        }
        registry
    }
}

/// Errors that can occur during workspace operations.
///
/// This mirrors the workspace error domain described in spec §69
/// (`HarnessError::Workspace(WorkspaceError)`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum WorkspaceError {
    /// The requested path does not exist in the workspace.
    #[error("path not found: {0}")]
    NotFound(String),

    /// The path exists but is not accessible (e.g. a directory treated as a file).
    #[error("path is not a file: {0}")]
    NotAFile(String),

    /// The operation was denied by a workspace policy.
    #[error("permission denied: {0}")]
    PermissionDenied(String),

    /// An internal, implementation-specific error occurred.
    #[error("internal workspace error: {0}")]
    Internal(String),
}

/// A query for searching the workspace.
///
/// The simplest form carries a literal substring pattern.  More sophisticated
/// queries (glob, regex, file-type filters) can be added as optional fields.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SearchQuery {
    /// The literal substring (or pattern) to search for.
    pub pattern: String,

    /// Optional file-path glob to restrict which files are searched.
    pub path_pattern: Option<String>,
}

/// A single match produced by a workspace search.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SearchMatch {
    /// The file path where the match was found.
    pub path: String,

    /// The 1-based line number of the match.
    pub line: usize,

    /// The matching line content (or a snippet thereof).
    pub line_content: String,
}

/// The result of a workspace search operation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SearchResult {
    /// The list of matches found.
    pub matches: Vec<SearchMatch>,

    /// Total number of matches (may exceed `matches.len()` if truncated).
    pub total: usize,

    /// Whether the result was truncated (e.g. by a limit).
    pub truncated: bool,
}

/// Summary status of a workspace.
///
/// Provides basic metadata about the workspace contents so that consumers
/// (frontends, budget calculations) can inspect state without walking the
/// entire file tree.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct WorkspaceStatus {
    /// The number of files currently tracked in the workspace.
    pub file_count: usize,

    /// The total size of all tracked files in bytes.
    pub total_size_bytes: u64,
}

/// Abstraction over a workspace backend — the files-and-search interface
/// that tools and context providers use to interact with project files.
///
/// The workspace **must** be injected into sessions and tool execution
/// contexts.  No code outside the workspace implementation should perform
/// direct filesystem I/O (spec §37).
///
/// ## Contract
///
/// 1. `read` returns the raw bytes at the given path, or
///    [`WorkspaceError::NotFound`] if the path does not exist.
///
/// 2. `write` creates or overwrites the file at the given path.
///
/// 3. `search` performs a content search according to the provided
///    [`SearchQuery`] and returns [`SearchResult`].
///
/// 4. `status` returns a snapshot of workspace metadata.
///

/// can trivially return immediately.
///

///
/// This trait is decorated with [`#[async_trait]`](async_trait) and
/// requires `Send + Sync`, which allows it to be stored as
/// `Arc<dyn Workspace>` and shared across tasks.
#[async_trait]
pub trait Workspace: Send + Sync {
    /// Read the full contents of the file at `path`.
    ///
    /// Returns the raw bytes on success, or a [`WorkspaceError`] if the
    /// path does not exist or cannot be read.
    async fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, WorkspaceError>;

    /// Write `data` to the file at `path`, creating or overwriting as
    /// needed.
    async fn write(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), WorkspaceError>;

    /// Search the workspace for content matching `query`.
    async fn search(&self, query: SearchQuery) -> Result<SearchResult, WorkspaceError>;

    /// Return a summary status of the workspace.
    async fn status(&self) -> Result<WorkspaceStatus, WorkspaceError>;
}

//! A scripted test-double backend that replays predetermined [`ExecutionEvent`]s
//! and returns a configured [`ExecutionResult`] or [`ExecutionError`].
//!
//! Use [`FakeBackend`] in unit tests and integration tests to exercise agent
//! runners, session logic, and tool orchestration without making real API calls.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_protocol::backend::{
    BackendCapabilities, BackendDescriptor, ExecutionContext, ExecutionError, ExecutionEvent,
    ExecutionRequest, ExecutionResult,
};
use harness_protocol::ids::BackendId;

use crate::traits::{ExecutionBackend, ExecutionEventSink};

/// A test-double [`ExecutionBackend`] that replays a scripted sequence of
/// [`ExecutionEvent`]s through the provided [`ExecutionEventSink`] and then
/// returns a predetermined [`ExecutionResult`] or [`ExecutionError`].
///
/// The backend respects the [`CancellationToken`]: if cancellation is
/// signalled at any point during event streaming, execution stops
/// immediately and returns [`ExecutionError::Cancelled`].
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```ignore
/// use harness_runtime::testing::fake_backend::FakeBackend;
/// use harness_protocol::backend::*;
/// use harness_protocol::ids::RequestId;
/// use harness_protocol::usage::{Cost, ModelUsage};
///
/// let request_id = RequestId::new();
/// let events = vec![
///     ExecutionEvent::TextDelta { request_id, delta: "Hello ".into() },
///     ExecutionEvent::TextDelta { request_id, delta: "world!".into() },
/// ];
///
/// let result = ExecutionResult {
///     request_id,
///     usage: ModelUsage::default(),
///     cost: Cost::default(),
///     finish_reason: "end_turn".into(),
/// };
///
/// let backend = FakeBackend::new(events, Ok(result));
/// ```
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct FakeBackend {
    /// The sequence of [`ExecutionEvent`]s streamed during [`execute`](ExecutionBackend::execute).
    pub scripted_events: Vec<ExecutionEvent>,
    /// The outcome returned after all scripted events have been sent.
    pub outcome: Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError>,
}

impl FakeBackend {
    /// Creates a new `FakeBackend` that will stream `scripted_events` through
    /// the event sink and then return `outcome`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    ///
    /// * `scripted_events` — Events to emit in order during execution.
    /// * `outcome` — The final `Ok(ExecutionResult)` or `Err(ExecutionError)`
    ///   returned once all events have been sent (or execution is cancelled).
    pub fn new(
        scripted_events: Vec<ExecutionEvent>,
        outcome: Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            scripted_events,
            outcome,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ExecutionBackend for FakeBackend {
    fn descriptor(&self) -> BackendDescriptor {
        BackendDescriptor {
            id: BackendId::new(),
            name: "fake".into(),
            description: "A test-double backend that replays scripted events.".into(),
            capabilities: BackendCapabilities {
                streaming: true,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        }
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> BackendCapabilities {
        let desc = self.descriptor();
        desc.capabilities
    }

    async fn execute(
        &self,
        _request: ExecutionRequest,
        _context: ExecutionContext,
        events: ExecutionEventSink,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError> {
        // Stream all scripted events, checking cancellation before each one.
        for event in &self.scripted_events {
            if cancel.is_cancelled() {
                // Drop the sender so the consumer sees the channel close.
                drop(events);
                return Err(ExecutionError::Cancelled);
            }

            // If the receiver has been dropped, treat it as cancellation.
            if events.send(event.clone()).is_err() {
                return Err(ExecutionError::Cancelled);
            }
        }

        // One last cancellation check before returning the outcome.
        if cancel.is_cancelled() {
            drop(events);
            return Err(ExecutionError::Cancelled);
        }

        self.outcome.clone()
    }
}

//! Runtime executor that drives a single agent's lifecycle by receiving
//! [`AgentCommand`]s from its mailbox, applying them to the agent's
//! deterministic state machine, and dispatching the resulting
//! [`AgentEffect`]s.
//!
//! ## Architecture
//!
//! ```text
//!                     ┌──────────────────┐
//!   mpsc::Receiver ◄──│   AgentCommand   │
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!                              ▼
//!                     ┌──────────────────┐
//!                     │  Agent::apply()  │  (pure, synchronous)
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!                     ┌────────▼─────────┐
//!                     │ Vec<AgentEffect> │
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!               ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
//!               ▼              ▼              ▼
//!         Emit           FinishRun        Other
//!     (broadcast)    (store result)    (delegated)
//! ```

use tokio::sync::{broadcast, mpsc};
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_protocol::commands::{AgentCommand, AgentResult};
use harness_protocol::effects::AgentEffect;
use harness_protocol::events::{AgentEventEnvelope, EventVisibility};
use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, EventId, Timestamp};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentTask  (spec §32 — mailbox primitive)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Mailbox and lifecycle primitives for driving a single agent.
///
/// This struct bundles the communication channels needed to send commands
/// to an agent, receive its events, and cancel its execution.
///
/// # Channel semantics
///
/// * **`commands`** (`mpsc::Receiver`) — the inbound command stream.  The
///   runner reads from this channel in a loop.  When the sender half is
///   dropped, the channel yields `None`, which causes the runner to exit.
///
/// * **`events`** (`broadcast::Sender`) — the outbound event bus.  Every
///   [`AgentEventEnvelope`] produced by the agent is published here.
///   Multiple subscribers (session bus, UI, logging) can independently
///   consume the stream.
///
/// * **`cancel`** (`CancellationToken`) — cooperative shutdown signal.
///   When triggered while the runner is waiting for a command, the runner
///   exits its event loop immediately.
pub struct AgentTask {
    /// The agent this task is associated with.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// Incoming command channel — the runner reads from this receiver.
    pub commands: mpsc::Receiver<AgentCommand>,
    /// Outgoing event channel — the runner publishes [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s
    /// on this sender so downstream consumers (session bus, UI, etc.) can
    /// observe agent activity.
    pub events: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    /// Cooperative cancellation token. When cancelled, the runner exits its
    /// event loop.
    pub cancel: CancellationToken,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentRunner  (spec §10)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Runtime executor that drives a single agent through its lifecycle.
///
/// The runner owns both the agent's deterministic core ([`Agent`]) and its
/// communication channels ([`AgentTask`]).  It runs an async event loop:
///
/// 1. Wait for the next [`AgentCommand`] from the mailbox (or a cancellation
///    signal).
/// 2. Apply the command to the agent via [`Agent::apply`] — a pure,
///    synchronous transition that mutates the agent's state and returns a
///    list of [`AgentEffect`]s.
/// 3. Interpret each effect:
///    * [`AgentEffect::Emit`] — wraps the inner [`AgentEvent`] in an
///      [`AgentEventEnvelope`] (filling in session/agent/sequence metadata)
///      and forwards it on the broadcast channel.
///    * [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`] — records the [`AgentResult`] so
///      callers can inspect it later (no external trait object required).
///    * All other effects — `ExecuteBackend`, `ExecuteTool`, `SpawnAgent`,
///      `RequestPermission`, `CancelBackend`, `CancelTool`, `CancelChild`,
///      `Persist` — require external trait objects or runtime coordination
///      and are **not** handled in this base implementation.
///
/// # State after completion
///
/// After a run finishes (success, failure, or cancellation), the agent
/// transitions to `Idle` or `Failed` and remains available to accept new
/// commands.  The runner therefore continues its event loop until the
/// command channel is closed or cancellation is requested.
pub struct AgentRunner {
    /// The agent's deterministic state machine.
    agent: Agent,
    /// The mailbox and lifecycle primitives.
    task: AgentTask,
    /// Monotonic counter scoped to this agent, used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of
    /// every emitted envelope.
    agent_sequence: u64,
    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    last_result: Option<AgentResult>,
}

impl AgentRunner {
    /// Create a new runner that owns the given `agent` and `task`.
    pub fn new(agent: Agent, task: AgentTask) -> Self {
        Self {
            agent,
            task,
            agent_sequence: 0,
            last_result: None,
        }
    }

    /// Run the event loop until the command channel closes or the
    /// cancellation token is triggered.
    ///
    /// After this method returns the caller can use
    /// [`into_agent`](Self::into_agent) to retrieve the agent (with its
    /// final state) or inspect [`last_result`](Self::last_result).
    pub async fn run(&mut self) {
        loop {
            tokio::select! {
                biased; // check cancellation first when both are ready

                _ = self.task.cancel.cancelled() => {
                    break;
                }

                cmd = self.task.commands.recv() => {
                    let Some(cmd) = cmd else {
                        // The sender was dropped; no more commands will arrive.
                        break;
                    };
                    self.handle_command(cmd).await;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Command → effect pipeline
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Apply a single command to the agent and dispatch every returned effect.
    async fn handle_command(&mut self, command: AgentCommand) {
        let effects = self.agent.apply(command);
        for effect in effects {
            self.handle_effect(effect).await;
        }
    }

    /// Interpret a single effect returned by the agent core.
    async fn handle_effect(&mut self, effect: AgentEffect) {
        match effect {
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Emit — wrap in an envelope and broadcast to subscribers
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::Emit { event } => {
                let envelope = AgentEventEnvelope {
                    event_id: EventId::new(),
                    session_id: self.agent.session_id,
                    agent_id: self.agent.id,
                    parent_agent_id: self.agent.parent_id,
                    run_id: self.agent.state.active_run,
                    agent_sequence: self.agent_sequence,
                    session_sequence: None, // assigned by session bus later
                    timestamp: Timestamp::now(),
                    visibility: EventVisibility::User,
                    event,
                };
                self.agent_sequence += 1;

                // `send` returns an error only when there are no active
                // receivers — that is a normal condition (e.g., no UI is
                // subscribed), so we silently ignore it.
                let _ = self.task.events.send(envelope);
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // FinishRun — store the result; the agent is still alive
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::FinishRun { result } => {
                self.last_result = Some(result);
                // The run is finished, but the agent can still accept new
                // commands (StartRun, Cancel, etc.).
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Unhandled effects — require external coordination
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            //
            // The following effects all require some form of external trait
            // object (e.g., an ExecutionBackend, ToolExecutor, PermissionUI,
            // SessionStore) that is outside the scope of this base loop.
            //
            // Downstream runners should extend or override handle_effect to
            // provide the necessary dispatch for these variants.
            AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend { .. }
            | AgentEffect::ExecuteTool { .. }
            | AgentEffect::SpawnAgent { .. }
            | AgentEffect::RequestPermission { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelBackend { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelTool { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelChild { .. }
            | AgentEffect::Persist { .. } => {
                // Intentionally a no-op in the base implementation.
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Accessors
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Shared reference to the inner agent (e.g. for inspecting state).
    pub fn agent(&self) -> &Agent {
        &self.agent
    }

    /// Mutable reference to the inner agent (e.g. for pre-populating state
    /// before the loop starts).
    pub fn agent_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Agent {
        &mut self.agent
    }

    /// Consume the runner and return the owned agent with its final state.
    pub fn into_agent(self) -> Agent {
        self.agent
    }

    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    ///
    /// This is set each time the agent emits an [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`]
    /// effect, which happens at the end of every run (success, failure, or
    /// cancellation).
    pub fn last_result(&self) -> Option<&AgentResult> {
        self.last_result.as_ref()
    }

    /// The current monotonic agent-sequence counter.
    ///
    /// This is the value that will be used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of the
    /// *next* emitted envelope.
    pub fn agent_sequence(&self) -> u64 {
        self.agent_sequence
    }
}

//! Runtime executor that drives a single agent's lifecycle by receiving
//! [`AgentCommand`]s from its mailbox, applying them to the agent's
//! deterministic state machine, and dispatching the resulting
//! [`AgentEffect`]s.
//!
//! ## Architecture
//!
//! ```text
//!                     ┌──────────────────┐
//!   mpsc::Receiver ◄──│   AgentCommand   │
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!                              ▼
//!                     ┌──────────────────┐
//!                     │  Agent::apply()  │  (pure, synchronous)
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!                     ┌────────▼─────────┐
//!                     │ Vec<AgentEffect> │
//!                     └────────┬─────────┘
//!                              │
//!               ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
//!               ▼              ▼              ▼
//!         Emit           FinishRun        Other
//!     (broadcast)    (store result)    (delegated)
//! ```

use tokio::sync::{broadcast, mpsc};
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_protocol::commands::{AgentCommand, AgentResult};
use harness_protocol::effects::AgentEffect;
use harness_protocol::events::{AgentEventEnvelope, EventVisibility};
use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, EventId, Timestamp};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentTask  (spec §32 — mailbox primitive)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Mailbox and lifecycle primitives for driving a single agent.
///
/// This struct bundles the communication channels needed to send commands
/// to an agent, receive its events, and cancel its execution.
///
/// # Channel semantics
///
/// * **`commands`** (`mpsc::Receiver`) — the inbound command stream.  The
///   runner reads from this channel in a loop.  When the sender half is
///   dropped, the channel yields `None`, which causes the runner to exit.
///
/// * **`events`** (`broadcast::Sender`) — the outbound event bus.  Every
///   [`AgentEventEnvelope`] produced by the agent is published here.
///   Multiple subscribers (session bus, UI, logging) can independently
///   consume the stream.
///
/// * **`cancel`** (`CancellationToken`) — cooperative shutdown signal.
///   When triggered while the runner is waiting for a command, the runner
///   exits its event loop immediately.
pub struct AgentTask {
    /// The agent this task is associated with.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// Incoming command channel — the runner reads from this receiver.
    pub commands: mpsc::Receiver<AgentCommand>,
    /// Outgoing event channel — the runner publishes [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s
    /// on this sender so downstream consumers (session bus, UI, etc.) can
    /// observe agent activity.
    pub events: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    /// Cooperative cancellation token. When cancelled, the runner exits its
    /// event loop.
    pub cancel: CancellationToken,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentRunner  (spec §10)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Runtime executor that drives a single agent through its lifecycle.
///
/// The runner owns both the agent's deterministic core ([`Agent`]) and its
/// communication channels ([`AgentTask`]).  It runs an async event loop:
///
/// 1. Wait for the next [`AgentCommand`] from the mailbox (or a cancellation
///    signal).
/// 2. Apply the command to the agent via [`Agent::apply`] — a pure,
///    synchronous transition that mutates the agent's state and returns a
///    list of [`AgentEffect`]s.
/// 3. Interpret each effect:
///    * [`AgentEffect::Emit`] — wraps the inner [`AgentEvent`] in an
///      [`AgentEventEnvelope`] (filling in session/agent/sequence metadata)
///      and forwards it on the broadcast channel.
///    * [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`] — records the [`AgentResult`] so
///      callers can inspect it later (no external trait object required).
///    * All other effects — `ExecuteBackend`, `ExecuteTool`, `SpawnAgent`,
///      `RequestPermission`, `CancelBackend`, `CancelTool`, `CancelChild`,
///      `Persist` — require external trait objects or runtime coordination
///      and are **not** handled in this base implementation.
///
/// # State after completion
///
/// After a run finishes (success, failure, or cancellation), the agent
/// transitions to `Idle` or `Failed` and remains available to accept new
/// commands.  The runner therefore continues its event loop until the
/// command channel is closed or cancellation is requested.
pub struct AgentRunner {
    /// The agent's deterministic state machine.
    agent: Agent,
    /// The mailbox and lifecycle primitives.
    task: AgentTask,
    /// Monotonic counter scoped to this agent, used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of
    /// every emitted envelope.
    agent_sequence: u64,
    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    last_result: Option<AgentResult>,
}

impl AgentRunner {
    /// Create a new runner that owns the given `agent` and `task`.
    pub fn new(agent: Agent, task: AgentTask) -> Self {
        Self {
            agent,
            task,
            agent_sequence: 0,
            last_result: None,
        }
    }

    /// Run the event loop until the command channel closes or the
    /// cancellation token is triggered.
    ///
    /// After this method returns the caller can use
    /// [`into_agent`](Self::into_agent) to retrieve the agent (with its
    /// final state) or inspect [`last_result`](Self::last_result).
    pub async fn run(&mut self) {
        loop {
            tokio::select! {
                biased; // check cancellation first when both are ready

                _ = self.task.cancel.cancelled() => {
                    break;
                }

                cmd = self.task.commands.recv() => {
                    let Some(cmd) = cmd else {
                        // The sender was dropped; no more commands will arrive.
                        break;
                    };
                    self.handle_command(cmd).await;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Command → effect pipeline
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Apply a single command to the agent and dispatch every returned effect.
    async fn handle_command(&mut self, command: AgentCommand) {
        let effects = self.agent.apply(command);
        for effect in effects {
            self.handle_effect(effect).await;
        }
    }

    /// Interpret a single effect returned by the agent core.
    async fn handle_effect(&mut self, effect: AgentEffect) {
        match effect {
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Emit — wrap in an envelope and broadcast to subscribers
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::Emit { event } => {
                let envelope = AgentEventEnvelope {
                    event_id: EventId::new(),
                    session_id: self.agent.session_id,
                    agent_id: self.agent.id,
                    parent_agent_id: self.agent.parent_id,
                    run_id: self.agent.state.active_run,
                    agent_sequence: self.agent_sequence,
                    session_sequence: None, // assigned by session bus later
                    timestamp: Timestamp::now(),
                    visibility: EventVisibility::User,
                    event,
                };
                self.agent_sequence += 1;

                // `send` returns an error only when there are no active
                // receivers — that is a normal condition (e.g., no UI is
                // subscribed), so we silently ignore it.
                let _ = self.task.events.send(envelope);
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // FinishRun — store the result; the agent is still alive
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::FinishRun { result } => {
                self.last_result = Some(result);
                // The run is finished, but the agent can still accept new
                // commands (StartRun, Cancel, etc.).
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Unhandled effects — require external coordination
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            //
            // The following effects all require some form of external trait
            // object (e.g., an ExecutionBackend, ToolExecutor, PermissionUI,
            // SessionStore) that is outside the scope of this base loop.
            //
            // Downstream runners should extend or override handle_effect to
            // provide the necessary dispatch for these variants.
            AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend { .. }
            | AgentEffect::ExecuteTool { .. }
            | AgentEffect::SpawnAgent { .. }
            | AgentEffect::RequestPermission { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelBackend { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelTool { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelChild { .. }
            | AgentEffect::Persist { .. } => {
                // Intentionally a no-op in the base implementation.
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Accessors
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Shared reference to the inner agent (e.g. for inspecting state).
    pub fn agent(&self) -> &Agent {
        &self.agent
    }

    /// Mutable reference to the inner agent (e.g. for pre-populating state
    /// before the loop starts).
    pub fn agent_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Agent {
        &mut self.agent
    }

    /// Consume the runner and return the owned agent with its final state.
    pub fn into_agent(self) -> Agent {
        self.agent
    }

    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    ///
    /// This is set each time the agent emits an [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`]
    /// effect, which happens at the end of every run (success, failure, or
    /// cancellation).
    pub fn last_result(&self) -> Option<&AgentResult> {
        self.last_result.as_ref()
    }

    /// The current monotonic agent-sequence counter.
    ///
    /// This is the value that will be used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of the
    /// *next* emitted envelope.
    pub fn agent_sequence(&self) -> u64 {
        self.agent_sequence
    }
}
