/// Runtime executor that drives a single agent through its lifecycle.
///
/// The runner owns both the agent's deterministic core ([`Agent`]) and its
/// communication channels ([`AgentTask`]).  It runs an async event loop:
///
/// 1. Wait for the next [`AgentCommand`] from the mailbox (or a cancellation
///    signal).
/// 2. Apply the command to the agent via [`Agent::apply`] — a pure,
///    synchronous transition that mutates the agent's state and returns a
///    list of [`AgentEffect`]s.
/// 3. Interpret each effect:
///    * [`AgentEffect::Emit`] — wraps the inner [`AgentEvent`] in an
///      [`AgentEventEnvelope`] (filling in session/agent/sequence metadata)
///      and forwards it on the broadcast channel.
///    * [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`] — records the [`AgentResult`] so
///      callers can inspect it later, and releases the command sender
///      so the event loop can exit cleanly when no external senders remain.
///    * [`AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend`] — spawns the injected
///      [`ExecutionBackend`] with the given request, streams execution
///      events back as [`AgentCommand::BackendEvent`] commands, and
///      discards the final [`ExecutionResult`] (the agent processes the
///      terminal [`ExecutionEvent::Completed`] or [`ExecutionEvent::Error`]
///      event instead).
///    * [`AgentEffect::ExecuteTool`] — resolves the tool name in the
///      [`ToolRegistry`], spawns the executor on a background task, and
///      feeds the result back as [`AgentCommand::ToolCompleted`] or
///      [`AgentCommand::ToolFailed`].
///    * [`AgentEffect::CancelBackend`] — cancels the child token
///      associated with the active backend request, causing the
///      in-flight stream to abort.
///    * [`AgentEffect::CancelTool`] — cancels the child token
///      associated with the pending tool call.
///    * All other effects — `SpawnAgent`, `RequestPermission`, `Persist`,
///      `CancelChild` — require external trait objects or runtime
///      coordination and are **not** handled in this base implementation.
///
/// # Cancellation (spec §35)
///
/// The runner owns a [`RunCancellation`] that forms the root of a
/// hierarchical cancellation tree:
///
/// ```text
/// RunCancellation (root token)
///   ├── Backend call token  (used in dispatch_backend)
///   ├── Tool call token     (used in dispatch_tool)
///   └── Child agent token   (future use)
/// ```
///
/// When the root is cancelled (via [`RunCancellation::cancel`] or the
/// external [`CancellationToken`] from [`AgentTask`]), the runner:
///
/// 1. Applies [`AgentCommand::Cancel`] to the agent state machine,
///    which transitions the agent to `Cancelled` and emits the
///    appropriate effects (`CancelBackend`, `CancelTool`,
///    `StateChanged`, `Completed { outcome: Cancelled }`).
/// 2. Dispatches all resulting effects (which in turn cancel the
///    child tokens and broadcast terminal events).
/// 3. Exits the event loop.
///
/// # Channel lifecycle
///
/// The runner holds an optional sender half of the command channel
/// (`command_tx`).  While present, the runner can inject
/// [`AgentCommand::BackendEvent`] and [`AgentCommand::ToolCompleted`]
/// commands.  The sender is released in two situations:
///
/// * Immediately when the agent emits [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`] (after a
///   successful or failed run).
/// * After any command that leaves the agent with no active run
///   (`active_run == None`), such as [`AgentCommand::Cancel`].
///
/// Once released, the channel can close when the external sender is also
/// dropped, allowing the event loop to exit naturally.
///
/// # State after completion
///
/// After a run finishes (success, failure, or cancellation), the agent
/// transitions to `Idle` or `Failed` and remains available to accept new
/// commands.  The runner therefore continues its event loop until the
/// command channel is closed or cancellation is requested.
pub struct AgentRunner {
    /// The agent's deterministic state machine.
    agent: Agent,
    /// The mailbox and lifecycle primitives.
    task: AgentTask,
    /// Monotonic counter scoped to this agent, used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of
    /// every emitted envelope.
    agent_sequence: u64,
    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    last_result: Option<AgentResult>,
    /// The injected execution backend used to dispatch
    /// [`AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend`] effects.
    backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
    /// The tool registry used to resolve and dispatch
    /// [`AgentEffect::ExecuteTool`] effects.
    tool_registry: ToolRegistry,
    /// Optional sender half of the command channel, used by the runner to
    /// inject [`AgentCommand::BackendEvent`] and [`AgentCommand::ToolCompleted`]
    /// events back to itself.
    ///
    /// This is set to `Some(...)` when the runner is created and cleared
    /// when the agent has no active run (so the channel can close).
    command_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>>,
    /// Hierarchical cancellation scope for the current run (spec §35).
    ///
    /// Child tokens are derived for every backend and tool call.  When

impl AgentRunner {
    /// Create a new runner that owns the given `agent`, `task`, `backend`,
    /// `tool_registry`, and command sender.

    /// exit once the runner also releases its handle.

        task: AgentTask,
        backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
        tool_registry: ToolRegistry,
        command_tx: mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>,

        Self {
            agent,
            task,
            agent_sequence: 0,
            last_result: None,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            command_tx: Some(command_tx),
            run_cancel: RunCancellation::new(),

    /// Run the event loop until the command channel closes or the
    /// cancellation token is triggered.
    ///
    /// When the token fires while a run is active, the runner applies
    /// [`AgentCommand::Cancel`] to the agent (so the state machine
    /// transitions to `Cancelled`), dispatches the resulting effects,
    /// and then exits.
    ///
    /// After this method returns the caller can use
    /// [`into_agent`](Self::into_agent) to retrieve the agent (with its
    /// final state) or inspect [`last_result`](Self::last_result).
    pub async fn run(&mut self) {
        loop {
            tokio::select! {
                biased; // check cancellation first when both are ready

                _ = self.task.cancel.cancelled() => {
                    // Also cancel our internal root token so all child
                    // tokens (backend, tool) fire immediately.
                    self.run_cancel.cancel();

                    // If there is an active run, transition the agent
                    // through the state machine so it emits the proper
                    // Cancelled effects.
                    if self.agent.state.active_run.is_some() {
                        self.handle_command(AgentCommand::Cancel).await;

                    break;

                cmd = self.task.commands.recv() => {
                    let Some(cmd) = cmd else {

                        // no more commands will arrive.
                        break;

                    self.handle_command(cmd).await;

    // Command → effect pipeline
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Apply a single command to the agent and dispatch every returned effect.
    async fn handle_command(&mut self, command: AgentCommand) {
        let effects = self.agent.apply(command);
        for effect in effects {
            self.handle_effect(effect).await;

        // After all effects have been dispatched, release the command
        // sender if the agent no longer has an active run.  This covers
        // commands like Cancel that transition the agent to a terminal
        // state without emitting a FinishRun effect.
        if self.command_tx.is_some() && self.agent.state.active_run.is_none() {
            self.command_tx = None;

    /// Interpret a single effect returned by the agent core.
    async fn handle_effect(&mut self, effect: AgentEffect) {
        match effect {
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Emit — wrap in an envelope and broadcast to subscribers
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::Emit { event } => {
                let envelope = AgentEventEnvelope {
                    event_id: EventId::new(),
                    session_id: self.agent.session_id,
                    agent_id: self.agent.id,
                    parent_agent_id: self.agent.parent_id,
                    run_id: self.agent.state.active_run,
                    agent_sequence: self.agent_sequence,
                    session_sequence: None, // assigned by session bus later
                    timestamp: Timestamp::now(),
                    visibility: EventVisibility::User,
                    event,
                };
                self.agent_sequence += 1;

                // `send` returns an error only when there are no active
                // receivers — that is a normal condition (e.g., no UI is
                // subscribed), so we silently ignore it.
                let _ = self.task.events.send(envelope);
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // FinishRun — store the result and release the command sender
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::FinishRun { result } => {
                self.last_result = Some(result);
                // Drop our handle on the command sender so the channel can
                // close when the external sender is also dropped.  This
                // allows the event loop to exit naturally.
                self.command_tx = None;
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // ExecuteBackend — dispatch to the injected backend
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend { request } => {
                self.dispatch_backend(request).await;
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // ExecuteTool — resolve and dispatch via the ToolRegistry
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::ExecuteTool { request } => {
                self.dispatch_tool(request).await;
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // CancelBackend — cancel the child token for the active
            // backend request (spec §35)
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::CancelBackend { run_id } => {
                // The root token has already been cancelled (either by the
                // user or by the run loop when the external token fired).
                // Since all child tokens derive from the root, they are
                // already cancelled.  We cancel the root again for good
                // measure (idempotent).
                //
                // In a future phase where multiple concurrent backends
                // may exist, this arm should cancel a specific token
                // identified by `run_id`.
                let _ = run_id;
                self.run_cancel.cancel();
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // CancelTool — cancel the child token for a pending tool
            // (spec §35)
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            AgentEffect::CancelTool { call_id } => {
                // Same reasoning as CancelBackend: the root token's
                // cancellation propagates to all tool child tokens.
                let _ = call_id;
                self.run_cancel.cancel();
            }

            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            // Unhandled effects — require external coordination
            // ----------------------------------------------------------
            //
            // The following effects all require some form of external trait
            // object (e.g., a PermissionUI, SessionStore) that is outside
            // the scope of this base loop.
            //
            // Downstream runners should extend or override handle_effect to
            // provide the necessary dispatch for these variants.
            AgentEffect::SpawnAgent { .. }
            | AgentEffect::RequestPermission { .. }
            | AgentEffect::CancelChild { .. }
            | AgentEffect::Persist { .. } => {

            }
        }

    /// Dispatch an [`ExecutionRequest`] to the injected backend and forward
    /// every streamed [`ExecutionEvent`] back to the agent as a
    /// [`AgentCommand::BackendEvent`].
    ///
    /// This method creates an unbounded channel, spawns the backend execution
    /// on a separate tokio task, and then reads events from the channel
    /// receiver, forwarding each one through the runner's command sender.
    /// When the backend finishes (or the receiver is closed), forwarding
    /// stops.
    ///
    /// The final [`ExecutionResult`] returned by the backend is deliberately
    /// discarded — the agent state machine processes the terminal event
    /// ([`ExecutionEvent::Completed`] or [`ExecutionEvent::Error`]) that the
    /// backend streams as part of its event sequence.
    ///
    /// ## Cancellation
    ///
    /// A child token is derived from [`run_cancel`](Self::run_cancel) and
    /// passed to the backend.  When the run is cancelled, this token fires
    /// and the backend (if cooperative) aborts its work.
    async fn dispatch_backend(&self, request: ExecutionRequest) {

        let run_id = request.run_id;

        // Clone the pieces needed by the backend task.
        let backend = Arc::clone(&self.backend);
        // Derive a child token so cancellation of the run propagates
        // to this specific backend call.

        // concurrently with event forwarding.

                .execute(
                    request,
                    ExecutionContext {
                        max_tokens: None,
                        temperature: None,
                        stop_sequences: vec![],
                    },
                    tx,
                    cancel,
                )
                .await;
            // The result is intentionally discarded — the agent has already
            // processed the terminal event (Completed / Error) from the
            // event stream.
        });

        // Obtain a clone of the command sender to forward events.
        let Some(cmd_tx) = self.command_tx.as_ref() else {
            // No command sender available — events cannot be forwarded.
            return;
        };
        let cmd_tx = cmd_tx.clone();

        // Forward every execution event back to the agent as a BackendEvent
        // command.  When the stream ends or the command receiver is dropped,
        // we stop forwarding.
        while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await {
            if cmd_tx
                .send(AgentCommand::BackendEvent { run_id, event })
                .await
                .is_err()
            {
                // The receiver (our own event loop) was dropped — stop
                // forwarding.
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Resolve a tool by name in the [`ToolRegistry`], execute it on a
    /// background task, and feed the result back to the agent as a
    /// [`AgentCommand::ToolCompleted`] or [`AgentCommand::ToolFailed`].
    ///
    /// ## Resolution strategy
    ///
    /// The tool is looked up by its **name** (the `name` field of the
    /// [`ToolCall`](harness_protocol::tools::ToolCall)) via
    /// [`ToolRegistry::resolve`].  This name-based lookup performs a linear
    /// scan over all registered executors.  If no executor with a matching
    /// name is found, a [`ToolFailed`](AgentCommand::ToolFailed) command
    /// with [`ToolError::Internal`] is sent back immediately.
    ///
    /// ## Concurrency
    ///
    /// The tool executor's [`execute`](crate::traits::ToolExecutor::execute)
    /// method is called on a spawned tokio task so that concurrent tool
    /// calls do not block the runner's event loop.  Tool progress events
    /// are streamed through an unbounded channel and currently discarded;
    /// they may be forwarded to the agent in a future phase.
    ///
    /// ## Cancellation
    ///
    /// A child token is derived from [`run_cancel`](Self::run_cancel) and
    /// passed to the executor.  When the run is cancelled (or a
    /// [`CancelTool`](AgentEffect::CancelTool) effect is handled), this
    /// child token fires, allowing cooperative cancellation of the
    /// in-flight tool call.
    async fn dispatch_tool(&self, request: harness_protocol::effects::ToolRequest) {
        let call_id = request.call.id;
        let tool_name = request.call.name;
        let arguments = request.call.arguments;

        // Look up the executor by tool name.
        let executor = match self.tool_registry.resolve(&tool_name) {
            Some(executor) => Arc::clone(executor),
            None => {
                // Tool not found in the registry — send a failure back.
                if let Some(cmd_tx) = self.command_tx.as_ref() {
                    let _ = cmd_tx
                        .send(AgentCommand::ToolFailed {
                            call_id,
                            error: ToolError::Internal,
                        })
                        .await;
                }
                return;
            }
        };

        // Create an unbounded channel for tool progress events.
        // The receiver is discarded for now; progress may be forwarded
        // to the agent in a future phase.
        let (tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel();
        // Derive a child token so cancellation of the run propagates
        // to this specific tool call.
        let cancel = self.run_cancel.child_token();
        let context = ToolExecutionContext::new();

        // Clone the command sender for the spawned task.
        let Some(cmd_tx) = self.command_tx.as_ref() else {
            // No command sender available — cannot deliver the result.
            return;
        };
        let cmd_tx = cmd_tx.clone();

        // Spawn the tool execution on a background task so it can run
        // concurrently with the agent's event loop.
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            match executor.execute(context, arguments, tx, cancel).await {
                Ok(result) => {
                    let _ = cmd_tx
                        .send(AgentCommand::ToolCompleted { call_id, result })
                        .await;
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    let _ = cmd_tx
                        .send(AgentCommand::ToolFailed { call_id, error })
                        .await;
                }
            }
        });
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Accessors
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Shared reference to the inner agent (e.g. for inspecting state).
    pub fn agent(&self) -> &Agent {
        &self.agent
    }

    /// Mutable reference to the inner agent (e.g. for pre-populating state
    /// before the loop starts).
    pub fn agent_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Agent {
        &mut self.agent
    }

    /// Consume the runner and return the owned agent with its final state.
    pub fn into_agent(self) -> Agent {
        self.agent
    }

    /// The result of the most recently completed run, if any.
    ///
    /// This is set each time the agent emits an [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`]
    /// effect, which happens at the end of every run (success, failure, or
    /// cancellation).
    pub fn last_result(&self) -> Option<&AgentResult> {
        self.last_result.as_ref()
    }

    /// The current monotonic agent-sequence counter.
    ///
    /// This is the value that will be used for the
    /// [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence) field of the
    /// *next* emitted envelope.
    pub fn agent_sequence(&self) -> u64 {
        self.agent_sequence
    }

    /// Shared reference to the run cancellation scope.
    ///
    /// External code can call [`cancel`](RunCancellation::cancel) on this
    /// to request orderly cancellation of the current run.
    pub fn run_cancel(&self) -> &RunCancellation {
        &self.run_cancel
    }
}

        // Collect all broadcast events in order.

        while let Ok(envelope) = evt_rx.try_recv() {

    ///

    ///
    /// 1. A run is started, which dispatches a backend call.
    /// 2. While the backend is still processing, the cancellation token
    ///    is triggered.
    /// 3. The runner detects cancellation, applies `AgentCommand::Cancel`
    ///    to the agent state machine, transitions to `Cancelled`, and
    ///    broadcasts the terminal events.
    /// 4. No further events are emitted after the `Completed` event.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn cancel_token_mid_flight_transitions_to_cancelled() {
        // Create a FakeBackend that will still be in-flight when we cancel.
        // Give it events and wrap with a small delay so we have a window
        // to cancel mid-flight.
        let request_id = RequestId::new();
        let scripted_events = vec![
            ExecutionEvent::TextDelta {
                request_id,
                delta: "before cancel ".into(),
            },
            ExecutionEvent::Completed {
                request_id,
                result: ExecutionResult {
                    request_id,
                    usage: harness_protocol::usage::ModelUsage::default(),
                    cost: harness_protocol::usage::Cost::default(),
                    finish_reason: "end_turn".into(),
                },
            },
        ];

        let inner_backend = FakeBackend::new(
            scripted_events,
            Ok(ExecutionResult {
                request_id,
                usage: harness_protocol::usage::ModelUsage::default(),
                cost: harness_protocol::usage::Cost::default(),
                finish_reason: "end_turn".into(),
            }),
        );

        // Wrap with a delay so the backend is "blocking" — this gives us
        // time to cancel while the backend is still in-flight.
        let backend = Arc::new(DelayedBackend::new(
            inner_backend,
            Duration::from_millis(100),
        ));

        let (cmd_tx, cmd_rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(16);
        let (evt_tx, mut evt_rx) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel(64);
        let cancel = tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken::new();

        let task = AgentTask {
            id: AgentId::new(),
            commands: cmd_rx,
            events: evt_tx,
            cancel: cancel.clone(),
        };

        let tool_registry = ToolRegistry::new();
        let mut runner = AgentRunner::new(
            dummy_agent(),
            task,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            cmd_tx.clone(),
        );

            .send(AgentCommand::StartRun {
                input: UserInput {
                    text: "cancel this run".into(),
                    attachments: vec![],
                },
            })
            .await
            .expect("send StartRun");

        // Brief pause to let the runner enter the backend-dispatch path
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;

        // Cancel the token while the backend is still in-flight
        cancel.cancel();

        // Drop the external sender so the loop can exit
        drop(cmd_tx);

        // Run the loop — it will detect cancellation, apply Cancel to the
        // agent, dispatch effects (broadcasting terminal events), and exit.
        runner.run().await;

        // ---- Assertion 1: Agent transitioned to Cancelled ----
        assert_eq!(
            runner.agent().state.status,
            AgentStatus::Cancelled,
            "agent should be Cancelled after token-based cancellation"
        );

        // ---- Assertion 2: A result was recorded ----
        let result = runner
            .last_result()
            .expect("FinishRun should set last_result");
        assert!(!result.summary.is_empty(), "cancellation should produce a summary");

        // ---- Assertion 3: Event stream ends with Completed(Cancelled) ----
        let mut events: Vec<AgentEvent> = Vec::new();
        while let Ok(envelope) = evt_rx.try_recv() {
            events.push(envelope.event);
        }

        // The last broadcast event must be Completed { outcome: Cancelled }.
        let last_event = events.last().expect("should have at least one event");
        match last_event {
            AgentEvent::Completed {
                outcome: AgentOutcome::Cancelled,
            } => {} // expected
            other => panic!(
                "last broadcast event should be Completed(Cancelled), got {other:?}"
            ),
        }

        // ---- Assertion 4: The Completed(Cancelled) is the terminal event ----
        // It must be at the last position with nothing after it.
        let cancelled_idx = events
            .iter()
            .rposition(|e| {
                matches!(e, AgentEvent::Completed {
                    outcome: AgentOutcome::Cancelled
                })
            })
            .expect("Completed(Cancelled) must exist in event stream");
        assert_eq!(
            cancelled_idx,
            events.len() - 1,
            "nothing should appear after Completed(Cancelled)"
        );

        // ---- Assertion 5: RunCancellation was triggered ----
        assert!(runner.run_cancel().is_cancelled(), "run_cancel should be cancelled");
    }

            FakeBackend::new(
                vec![
                    ExecutionEvent::TextDelta {
                        request_id,
                        delta: "before ".into(),
                    },
                ],
                Ok(ExecutionResult {
                    request_id,
                    usage: harness_protocol::usage::ModelUsage::default(),
                    cost: harness_protocol::usage::Cost::default(),
                    finish_reason: "end_turn".into(),
                }),
            ),
            Duration::from_millis(100),
        ));

        let (evt_tx, mut evt_rx) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel(64);
        let cancel = tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken::new();

        let task = AgentTask {
            id: AgentId::new(),
            commands: cmd_rx,
            events: evt_tx,
            cancel: cancel.clone(),
        };

        let tool_registry = ToolRegistry::new();
        let mut runner = AgentRunner::new(
            dummy_agent(),
            task,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            cmd_tx.clone(),
        );

        cmd_tx
            .send(AgentCommand::StartRun {
                input: UserInput {
                    text: "test".into(),
                    attachments: vec![],
                },
            })
            .await
            .expect("send StartRun");

        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;

        runner.run_cancel().cancel();

        drop(cmd_tx);
        runner.run().await;

            runner.agent().state.status,
            AgentStatus::Cancelled,
            "agent should be Cancelled after RunCancellation cancel"
        );
        assert!(runner.last_result().is_some());

        while let Ok(envelope) = evt_rx.try_recv() {
            events.push(envelope.event);
        }
        let last_event = events.last().expect("should have events");
        assert!(
            matches!(last_event, AgentEvent::Completed {
                outcome: AgentOutcome::Cancelled
            }),
            "last event should be Completed(Cancelled)"

//! Session runtime — event bus, session state, and lifecycle.
//!
//! This module provides [`SessionEventBus`], the central aggregation point
//! that transforms per-agent [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s into a session-scoped
//! [`SessionEvent`] stream with monotonically increasing
//! [`session_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::session_sequence) values.
//!
//! It also provides [`SessionRuntime`] — the top-level executor that owns
//! a session's root agent runner, routes [`SessionCommand`]s to the agent,
//! and forwards agent events into the session stream (spec §6.2).
//!
//! ## Architecture (spec §40/§44)
//!
//! ```text
//! Agent
//!   ↓  AgentEventEnvelope (session_sequence: None)
//! SessionEventBus
//!   ├── assigns session_sequence
//!   ├── wraps in SessionEvent::Agent { event }
//!   └── broadcasts to subscribers
//!         ├── IDE
//!         ├── TUI
//!         ├── WebSocket
//!         ├── logging
//!         └── telemetry
//! ```
//!
//! ## SessionRuntime (spec §6.2)
//!
//! ```text
//! External caller
//!   │  SessionCommand::Prompt
//!   ▼
//! SessionRuntime
//!   ├── routes to AgentCommand::StartRun
//!   ├── spawns root AgentRunner (background task)
//!   ├── forwards agent events → SessionEventBus
//!   └── publishes SessionStarted / Completed lifecycle events
//! ```

use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_core::capabilities::AgentCapabilities;
use harness_protocol::backend::{BackendBinding, BackendReference};
use harness_protocol::commands::{AgentCommand, UserInput};
use harness_protocol::events::{AgentEvent, AgentEventEnvelope};
use harness_protocol::ids::{
    AgentId, ConfigurationId, IntegrationId, PermissionId, RunId, SessionId,
};
use harness_protocol::usage::{AgentBudget, SessionUsageSnapshot};

use crate::agent_runner::{AgentRunner, AgentTask};
use crate::traits::{ExecutionBackend, ToolRegistry, Workspace};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionStatus
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The lifecycle status of a session.
///
/// Mirrors the session state machine transitions defined in spec §44.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum SessionStatus {
    /// The session has been created but has not yet started processing.
    Starting,
    /// The session is actively processing (accepting prompts, running agents).
    Running,
    /// The session has been paused (agents are suspended).
    Paused,
    /// The session completed normally.
    Completed,
    /// The session terminated with an unrecoverable error.
    Failed,
    /// The session was cancelled before completion.
    Cancelled,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionError
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A structured error representing a session-level failure.
///
/// This is distinct from agent-level or backend-level errors — it indicates
/// that the session itself (rather than an individual agent within it) has
/// encountered an unrecoverable condition.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SessionError {
    /// A human-readable description of what went wrong.
    pub message: String,
    /// A machine-readable error code (e.g. `"SESSION_CRASHED"`, `"TIMEOUT"`).
    pub code: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentDescriptor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A lightweight description of an agent within a session.
///
/// Used in [`SessionEvent::AgentAdded`] to notify consumers when a new agent
/// (root or child) is registered.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AgentDescriptor {
    /// The unique identifier of the agent.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// The parent agent's identifier, if any. Root agents have `None`.
    pub parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    /// A human-readable name or label for the agent (e.g. `"root"`, `"research"`).
    pub name: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionEvent
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Events emitted by a session, aggregated from all agents within that session.
///
/// The session is the preferred frontend subscription boundary (spec §44).
/// A frontend subscribes to one session and automatically receives events
/// for the root agent and all descendants through the [`Agent`](Self::Agent)
/// variant.
///
/// Every [`AgentEventEnvelope`] that passes through the session bus receives
/// a monotonically increasing [`session_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::session_sequence)
/// so that consumers can reconstruct a total order across all agents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SessionEvent {
    /// The session has started and is ready to accept commands.
    SessionStarted,

    /// The session's [`SessionStatus`] changed.
    StatusChanged {
        /// The new status of the session.
        status: SessionStatus,
    },

    /// An event originating from one of the session's agents.
    ///
    /// The embedded [`AgentEventEnvelope`] carries all routing metadata
    /// (`session_id`, `agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`, `run_id`) as well as
    /// the per-agent and per-session sequence numbers.
    Agent {
        /// The fully qualified agent event with session-level sequencing.
        event: AgentEventEnvelope,
    },

    /// A new agent was added to the session (root or child).
    AgentAdded {
        /// A descriptor of the newly added agent.
        agent: AgentDescriptor,
    },

    /// An agent was removed from the session (e.g. after completion or failure).
    AgentRemoved {
        /// The identifier of the agent that was removed.
        agent_id: AgentId,
    },

    /// Session-level usage metrics were updated.
    UsageUpdated {
        /// A snapshot of the session's aggregated usage.
        usage: SessionUsageSnapshot,
    },

    /// The session completed successfully.
    Completed,

    /// The session failed with an unrecoverable error.
    Failed {
        /// Details about the failure.
        error: SessionError,
    },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionEventBus
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Aggregates one or more [`AgentRunner`] broadcast channels into a single
/// [`SessionEvent`] stream, assigning monotonically increasing
/// `session_sequence` values to every [`AgentEventEnvelope`] that passes
/// through (spec §40/§44).
///
/// # How it works
///
/// The bus maintains an atomic 64-bit counter that is incremented for each
/// agent event forwarded.  It does **not** own the agent-runner subscriptions
/// directly — callers (typically the [`SessionRuntime`] event loop) invoke
/// [`forward_agent_event`](Self::forward_agent_event) whenever they receive
/// an envelope from an agent runner's broadcast channel, or use the
/// convenience [`spawn_agent_forwarder`](Self::spawn_agent_forwarder) method
/// to hand that responsibility off to a background task.
///
/// # Thread safety
///
/// All methods take `&self` because the sequence counter is an `AtomicU64`.
/// This allows the bus to be shared across multiple forwarding tasks or used
/// from a single event loop without a mutex.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(256);
/// let mut rx = bus.subscribe();
///
/// // Forward an agent event (synchronous)
/// bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);
///
/// // Or spawn a background forwarder for an agent runner's broadcast
/// let arc_bus = Arc::new(bus);
/// SessionEventBus::spawn_agent_forwarder(&arc_bus, agent_runner_receiver);
/// ```
pub struct SessionEventBus {
    /// The output channel — subscribers receive [`SessionEvent`]s.
    output: broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent>,
    /// Monotonic counter incremented for every agent event forwarded.
    /// Atomic so that `forward_agent_event` can be called concurrently
    /// from multiple spawned forwarding tasks.
    session_sequence: AtomicU64,
}

impl SessionEventBus {
    /// Create a new `SessionEventBus` that publishes to the given sender.
    ///
    /// The caller provides the [`broadcast::Sender`] so that multiple
    /// components can share the same underlying channel if needed.
    /// Use [`with_capacity`](Self::with_capacity) for a simpler standalone
    /// creation pattern.
    pub fn new(output: broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent>) -> Self {
        Self {
            output,
            session_sequence: AtomicU64::new(0),
        }
    }

    /// Create a `SessionEventBus` with a freshly allocated broadcast channel
    /// of the given capacity.
    ///
    /// This is the simplest construction — the bus owns the only sender, and
    /// callers subscribe via [`subscribe`](Self::subscribe).
    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let (tx, _) = broadcast::channel(capacity);
        Self::new(tx)
    }

    /// Subscribe to the session-level event stream.
    ///
    /// Returns a [`broadcast::Receiver`] that will receive every
    /// [`SessionEvent`] published on this bus, starting from the most recent
    /// messages still in the buffer (or none if the buffer has already been
    /// exhausted).
    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<SessionEvent> {
        self.output.subscribe()
    }

    /// Return a clone of the inner sender, allowing external code to
    /// publish events directly (e.g. for testing or for forwarding from
    /// other sources).
    pub fn sender(&self) -> broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent> {
        self.output.clone()
    }

    /// Forward an [`AgentEventEnvelope`] from an agent runner into the
    /// session stream.
    ///
    /// This method:
    /// 1. Assigns the next `session_sequence` value to the envelope.
    /// 2. Wraps it in [`SessionEvent::Agent`].
    /// 3. Publishes it on the output broadcast channel.
    ///
    /// If there are no active subscribers, the event is silently dropped
    /// (this is intentional — the bus does not buffer for absent consumers).
    pub fn forward_agent_event(&self, mut envelope: AgentEventEnvelope) {
        let seq = self.session_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        envelope.session_sequence = Some(seq);
        let _ = self.output.send(SessionEvent::Agent { event: envelope });
    }

    /// Publish a lifecycle [`SessionEvent`] that does not originate from a
    /// specific agent (e.g. [`SessionStarted`](SessionEvent::SessionStarted),
    /// [`Completed`](SessionEvent::Completed)).
    ///
    /// Note: this method does **not** assign a `session_sequence` because
    /// non-agent events are not sequenced at the agent-envelope level.
    /// They are delivered in publication order relative to agent events due
    /// to the sequential nature of the broadcast channel.
    ///
    /// If there are no active subscribers, the event is silently dropped.
    pub fn publish(&self, event: SessionEvent) {
        let _ = self.output.send(event);
    }

    /// Spawn a background task that forwards all events from a single
    /// agent runner's [`broadcast::Receiver`] into this session bus.
    ///
    /// The caller provides a reference-counted bus so the spawned task can
    /// hold its own reference.  The returned [`tokio::task::JoinHandle`] can
    /// be used to monitor or cancel the forwarding task.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The forwarding task runs until the agent runner's broadcast sender
    /// is dropped (which causes `recv()` to return `Err(Closed)`) or until
    /// the task is cancelled.  If the receiver lags behind, the task silently
    /// drops the missed events and continues.
    ///
    /// # Example
    ///
    /// ```rust,ignore
    /// let bus = Arc::new(SessionEventBus::with_capacity(256));
    /// let handle = SessionEventBus::spawn_agent_forwarder(&bus, agent_receiver);
    /// ```
    pub fn spawn_agent_forwarder(
        bus: &Arc<Self>,
        agent_receiver: broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    ) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> {
        let bus = Arc::clone(bus);
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            loop {
                match agent_receiver.recv().await {
                    Ok(envelope) => {
                        bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);
                    }
                    Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => {
                        // The agent runner shut down; no more events.
                        break;
                    }
                    Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => {
                        // We missed some events.  Best-effort forwarder —
                        // continue with the next available event.
                        continue;
                    }
                }
            }
        })
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The live session runtime, owning the root agent runner and event bus.
///
/// `SessionRuntime` ties together the session's state, its injected backend
/// and workspace, and the event aggregation bus.  On construction it:
///
/// 1. Creates the root [`Agent`] and wraps it in an [`AgentRunner`].
/// 2. Spawns the agent runner on a background tokio task.
/// 3. Spawns a run-loop task that:
///    - Publishes [`SessionEvent::SessionStarted`].
///    - Receives [`SessionCommand`]s and routes [`Prompt`](SessionCommand::Prompt)
///      to [`AgentCommand::StartRun`].
///    - Forwards agent events through [`SessionEventBus::forward_agent_event`].
///    - Publishes [`SessionEvent::Completed`] when the agent completes.
///
/// # Architecture
///
/// ```text
///           SessionCommand::Prompt
///                    │
///                    ▼
///        SessionRuntime run-loop
///                    │
///         ┌──────────┼──────────────┐
///         ▼          ▼              ▼
///   AgentCommand  AgentEvent    SessionEvent::Completed
///   ::StartRun    → forwarded    (terminal)
///         │
///         ▼
///   AgentRunner (bg task)
///         │
///         ├── FakeBackend (test) / real backend
///         └── events broadcast
/// ```
pub struct SessionRuntime {
    /// The durable session identity and metadata.
    pub state: SessionState,

    /// The execution backend injected for this session.
    pub default_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,

    /// The workspace injected for this session.
    pub workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,

    /// The event bus that aggregates agent events into the session stream.
    pub event_bus: SessionEventBus,

    /// Sender for [`SessionCommand`]s — the run loop receives on the
    /// corresponding receiver.
    command_tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<SessionCommand>,
}

impl SessionRuntime {
    /// Create a new `SessionRuntime` and start its background run loop.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    ///
    /// * `state` — the session's durable identity.
    /// * `default_backend` — the backend all agent runs in this session
    ///   will use.
    /// * `workspace` — the workspace injected for file I/O.
    /// * `event_bus` — the bus onto which session events are published.
    /// * `system_prompt` — the system instructions for the root agent.
    /// * `capabilities` — the capabilities granted to the root agent.
    /// * `tool_registry` — the runtime-wide tool registry.
    /// * `budget` — the budget constraints for the root agent.
    pub fn new(
        state: SessionState,
        default_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
        workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
        event_bus: SessionEventBus,
        system_prompt: String,
        capabilities: AgentCapabilities,
        tool_registry: ToolRegistry,
        budget: AgentBudget,
    ) -> Self {
        // ── Command channels ──────────────────────────────────────────
        let (command_tx, command_rx) =
            tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<SessionCommand>(32);
        let (agent_cmd_tx, agent_cmd_rx) =
            tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<AgentCommand>(32);
        let (agent_evt_tx, agent_evt_rx) =
            tokio::sync::broadcast::channel::<AgentEventEnvelope>(256);

        // ── Root agent ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        let agent = Agent::new(
            state.root_agent_id,
            state.id,
            None, // root agent has no parent
            system_prompt,
            BackendBinding {
                reference: BackendReference {
                    integration: IntegrationId::new(),
                    configuration: ConfigurationId::new(),
                    model: None,
                },
                descriptor: default_backend.descriptor(),
            },
            capabilities,
            budget,
        );

        // ── Agent task (mailbox) ──────────────────────────────────────
        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
        let agent_task = AgentTask {
            id: state.root_agent_id,
            commands: agent_cmd_rx,
            events: agent_evt_tx,
            cancel: cancel.clone(),
        };

        let agent_runner = AgentRunner::new(
            agent,
            agent_task,
            default_backend.clone(),
            tool_registry,
            agent_cmd_tx.clone(),
        );

        // Spawn the agent runner on a background task.
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            agent_runner.run().await;
        });

        // ── Session run loop ──────────────────────────────────────────
        // Wrap the event bus in an Arc so the spawned loop can share it.
        let bus = Arc::new(event_bus);
        Self::spawn_run_loop(
            Arc::clone(&bus),
            command_rx,
            agent_cmd_tx,
            agent_evt_rx,
            cancel,
        );

        // Extract the plain event bus back from the Arc.
        // At this point the Arc has exactly two references: the local
        // `bus` and the one moved into `spawn_run_loop`'s closure.
        // We unwrap the local one and drop it — the spawned task keeps
        // its own clone alive.
        let inner_bus = Arc::try_unwrap(bus)
            .expect("SessionRuntime: event_bus Arc must have exactly one strong ref after spawn");

        Self {
            state,
            default_backend,
            workspace,
            event_bus: inner_bus,
            command_tx,
        }
    }

    /// Spawn the background run-loop task.
    ///
    /// This task:
    /// 1. Publishes [`SessionEvent::SessionStarted`].
    /// 2. Listens for [`SessionCommand`]s and [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s.
    /// 3. Routes [`SessionCommand::Prompt`] to [`AgentCommand::StartRun`].
    /// 4. Forwards agent events through the session bus.
    /// 5. Publishes [`SessionEvent::Completed`] when the agent finishes.
    /// 6. Publishes [`SessionEvent::Failed`] when the agent fails.
    fn spawn_run_loop(
        bus: Arc<SessionEventBus>,
        mut command_rx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<SessionCommand>,
        agent_cmd_tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>,
        mut agent_evt_rx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope>,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            // Signal that the session is live.
            bus.publish(SessionEvent::SessionStarted);

            loop {
                tokio::select! {
                    // ── Session command received ──────────────────────
                    cmd = command_rx.recv() => {
                        let Some(cmd) = cmd else {
                            // All senders dropped — shut down.
                            break;
                        };

                        match cmd {
                            SessionCommand::Prompt(input) => {
                                // Route Prompt → StartRun.
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::StartRun { input })
                                    .await;
                            }
                            SessionCommand::CancelRun { .. }
                            | SessionCommand::CancelAgent { .. } => {
                                // Cancel the entire run/agent hierarchy.
                                cancel.cancel();
                            }
                            SessionCommand::PauseAgent { .. } => {
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::Pause)
                                    .await;
                            }
                            SessionCommand::ResumeAgent { .. } => {
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::Resume)
                                    .await;
                            }
                            // Permission routing is deferred to a later phase.
                            SessionCommand::ApprovePermission { .. }
                            | SessionCommand::RejectPermission { .. } => {}
                        }
                    }

                    // ── Agent event received ──────────────────────────
                    agent_result = agent_evt_rx.recv() => {
                        match agent_result {
                            Ok(envelope) => {
                                // Check for terminal agent events *before*
                                // forwarding so we can also emit the
                                // session-level terminal event.
                                let is_completed = matches!(
                                    envelope.event,
                                    AgentEvent::Completed { .. }
                                );
                                let is_failed = matches!(
                                    envelope.event,
                                    AgentEvent::Failed { .. }
                                );

                                // Assign session_sequence and publish.
                                bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);

                                // Publish session-level terminal event.
                                if is_completed {
                                    bus.publish(SessionEvent::Completed);
                                    break;
                                }
                                if is_failed {
                                    bus.publish(SessionEvent::Failed {
                                        error: SessionError {
                                            message: "Agent run failed".into(),
                                            code: "AGENT_FAILED".into(),
                                        },
                                    });
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                            Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => {
                                // Agent runner shut down — no more events.
                                break;
                            }
                            Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => {
                                // We missed some events — best-effort
                                // continue with the next one.
                                continue;
                            }
                        }
                    }

                    // ── Cancellation requested ────────────────────────
                    _ = cancel.cancelled() => break,
                }
            }
        });
    }

    /// Returns a clone of the command sender, allowing external code to
    /// send [`SessionCommand`]s to this session.
    pub fn command_tx(&self) -> tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<SessionCommand> {
        self.command_tx.clone()
    }

    /// Send a [`SessionCommand`] to the session's run loop.
    ///
    /// Returns an error if the run loop has already shut down (the receiver
    /// was dropped).
    pub async fn send_command(
        &self,
        command: SessionCommand,
    ) -> Result<(), tokio::sync::mpsc::error::SendError<SessionCommand>> {
        self.command_tx.send(command).await
    }
}

        let first_agent_idx = events

            .position(|e| matches!(e, SessionEvent::Agent { .. }));
        let completed_idx = events
            .iter()
            .rposition(|e| matches!(e, SessionEvent::Completed));

        if let Some(agent_start) = first_agent_idx {
            assert!(
                0 < agent_start,
                "SessionStarted (index 0) should precede all Agent events"
            );
        }

        if let Some(done) = completed_idx {
            assert_eq!(
                done,
                events.len() - 1,
                "Completed must be the last event in the stream"
            );
        }

## Summary of Changes

### 1. `crates/harness-runtime/src/runtime.rs` — Session-level cancellation command translation

**The core translation change** in `spawn_run_loop()`:

- **`SessionCommand::CancelRun`** (previously `cancel.cancel()` only) now sends `AgentCommand::Cancel` through the agent command channel **before** cancelling the token. This triggers an orderly state-machine transition in the agent runner (via `Agent::apply(AgentCommand::Cancel)` → `CancelBackend`/`CancelTool` effects → `RunCancellation.cancel()`).

- **`SessionCommand::CancelAgent`** similarly now sends `AgentCommand::Cancel`.

- **Two new integration tests:**
  - `cancel_run_translates_to_agent_command_cancel` — sends `CancelRun` mid-run, asserts the stream produces `SessionStarted` → `Agent` events → `Completed`
  - `cancel_agent_translates_to_agent_command_cancel` — sends `CancelAgent`, asserts the same terminal flow

### 2. `crates/harness-runtime/src/cancellation.rs` — `RunCancellation.child_of()` constructor

Added the **`child_of(parent: &CancellationToken) -> Self`** constructor to `RunCancellation`:

- Creates a cancellation scope that is a child of the given parent token
- When the parent cancels, the child scope cancels (propagates downward)
- When the child cancels, the parent does **not** cancel (one-way isolation)
- Useful for session→agent hierarchical cancellation: session passes its token as parent, agent runs derive child scopes

**Two new tests:**
- `child_of_inherits_parent_cancellation` — cancelling parent propagates to child
- `child_of_does_not_cancel_parent` — cancelling child does not propagate to parent

### Wiring flow (complete)

```
SessionCommand::CancelRun/CancelAgent
  → SessionRuntime run-loop
    → agent_cmd_tx.send(AgentCommand::Cancel) ... translation
    → cancel.cancel()                           ... safety net
      → AgentTask.cancel fires
        → AgentRunner.run() detects cancellation
          → agent.apply(AgentCommand::Cancel)
            → effects: CancelBackend/CancelTool
              → run_cancel.cancel()
                → all child tokens fire
                  → backend/tool tasks abort
```

//! [`SessionEvent`] stream with monotonically increasing
//! [`session_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::session_sequence) values.
//!
//! It also provides [`SessionRuntime`] — the top-level executor that owns
//! a session's root agent runner, routes [`SessionCommand`]s to the agent,
//! and forwards agent events into the session stream (spec §6.2).
//!
//! ## Architecture (spec §40/§44)
//!
//! ```text
//! Agent
//!   ↓  AgentEventEnvelope (session_sequence: None)
//! SessionEventBus
//!   ├── assigns session_sequence
//!   ├── wraps in SessionEvent::Agent { event }
//!   └── broadcasts to subscribers
//!         ├── IDE
//!         ├── TUI
//!         ├── WebSocket
//!         ├── logging
//!         └── telemetry
//! ```
//!
//! ## SessionRuntime (spec §6.2)
//!
//! ```text
//! External caller
//!   │  SessionCommand::Prompt
//!   ▼
//! SessionRuntime
//!   ├── routes to AgentCommand::StartRun
//!   ├── spawns root AgentRunner (background task)
//!   ├── forwards agent events → SessionEventBus
//!   └── publishes SessionStarted / Completed lifecycle events
//! ```

use tokio::sync::broadcast;
