//! Hierarchical cancellation for agent runs (spec §35).
//!
//! Tokio's [`CancellationToken`] forms the backbone — we wrap it in a
//! [`RunCancellation`] scoped to a single agent run.  Child tokens are
//! derived for each backend call, tool call, or child agent spawned
//! during the run.  Cancelling the root propagates to all children
//! automatically.
//!
//! # Hierarchy
//!
//! ```text
//! Session token
//!   └── Agent run token (RunCancellation)
//!         ├── Backend call token
//!         ├── Tool call token
//!         └── Child agent token
//! ```
//!
//! When the run token is cancelled, all child tokens are immediately
//! cancelled, causing in-flight backend streams, tool executors, and
//! child agents to cease work (spec §35: "backend streams, tools,
//! processes").
//!
//! # Session-level integration
//!
//! The session runtime creates a [`CancellationToken`] per session that is
//! wired into the [`AgentTask`](crate::agent_runner::AgentTask) mailbox.
//! When the session receives a [`CancelRun`](crate::runtime::SessionCommand::CancelRun)
//! or [`CancelAgent`](crate::runtime::SessionCommand::CancelAgent) command,
//! the run-loop translates it into [`AgentCommand::Cancel`](harness_protocol::commands::AgentCommand::Cancel),
//! which flows through the agent state machine and triggers the
//! [`RunCancellation`] inside the runner.  The session also cancels its
//! own token as a safety net so that any in-flight backend or tool calls
//! are aborted immediately.

use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

/// A hierarchical cancellation scope for a single agent run.
///
/// Create one per call to [`AgentRunner::run`] or per
/// [`AgentCommand::StartRun`].  The root token is used in the
/// runner's `tokio::select!` loop; child tokens are given to
/// every spawned backend or tool execution so that cancelling the
/// run automatically stops all in-flight work.
///
/// # Session-level usage
///
/// A session can create a [`RunCancellation`] that is a child of the
/// session's own [`CancellationToken`] via [`child_of`](Self::child_of).
/// This lets the session cancel all agent runs when it shuts down,
/// while still allowing individual agent runs to be cancelled
/// independently.
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```ignore
/// use harness_runtime::cancellation::RunCancellation;
///
/// let run = RunCancellation::new();
///
/// // Hand a child token to a backend call
/// let backend_handle = run.child_token();
/// tokio::spawn(async move { backend.execute(..., backend_handle).await });
///
/// // Cancel the run — the backend task will receive cancellation
/// run.cancel();
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RunCancellation {
    /// The root token for this run.  Cancelling it propagates to
    /// every child token created via [`child_token`](Self::child_token).
    root: CancellationToken,
}

impl RunCancellation {
    /// Create a new, un-cancelled run cancellation scope.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            root: CancellationToken::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Create a [`RunCancellation`] that is a child of the given parent
    /// [`CancellationToken`].
    ///
    /// When the parent token is cancelled, this run cancellation is also
    /// cancelled (and vice versa: cancelling this scope does **not**
    /// cancel the parent).
    ///
    /// This is useful for session-level orchestration: the session passes
    /// its own token as the parent so that shutting down the session
    /// propagates to all active agent runs.
    pub fn child_of(parent: &CancellationToken) -> Self {
        Self {
            root: parent.child_token(),
        }
    }

    /// Derive a new child token for a backend or tool execution.
    ///
    /// Multiple calls return independent child tokens.  Cancelling
    /// any one of them does **not** affect the root or other children;
    /// cancelling the root cancels all children.
    pub fn child_token(&self) -> CancellationToken {
        self.root.child_token()
    }

    /// Cancel the entire run.
    ///
    /// All existing child tokens (backend, tool, child agent) are
    /// immediately cancelled.  New child tokens created after this
    /// call will also start in the cancelled state.
    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.root.cancel();
    }

    /// Returns `true` if the run (or any ancestor) has been cancelled.
    pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool {
        self.root.is_cancelled()
    }

    /// Returns a clone of the root token, suitable for use in the
    /// runner's `tokio::select!` loop to detect cancellation.
    pub fn token(&self) -> CancellationToken {
        self.root.clone()
    }
}

impl Default for RunCancellation {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A fresh `RunCancellation` is not cancelled.
    #[test]
    fn not_cancelled_by_default() {
        let run = RunCancellation::new();
        assert!(!run.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// Cancelling the root marks it as cancelled.
    #[test]
    fn cancel_marks_cancelled() {
        let run = RunCancellation::new();
        run.cancel();
        assert!(run.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// Child tokens share the cancellation state of the root.
    #[test]
    fn child_token_inherits_cancellation() {
        let run = RunCancellation::new();
        let child = run.child_token();
        assert!(!child.is_cancelled());

        run.cancel();
        assert!(child.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// Multiple child tokens are all cancelled when the root is cancelled.
    #[test]
    fn multiple_children_all_cancelled() {
        let run = RunCancellation::new();
        let c1 = run.child_token();
        let c2 = run.child_token();

        run.cancel();
        assert!(c1.is_cancelled());
        assert!(c2.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// Cloning `RunCancellation` shares the same root token.
    #[test]
    fn clone_shares_root() {
        let run_a = RunCancellation::new();
        let run_b = run_a.clone();

        run_a.cancel();
        assert!(run_b.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// New children created after cancellation are already cancelled.
    #[test]
    fn child_token_after_cancel_is_cancelled() {
        let run = RunCancellation::new();
        run.cancel();
        let child = run.child_token();
        assert!(child.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// `child_of` creates a scope that inherits from the parent token.
    #[test]
    fn child_of_inherits_parent_cancellation() {
        let parent = CancellationToken::new();
        let run = RunCancellation::child_of(&parent);
        assert!(!run.is_cancelled());

        parent.cancel();
        assert!(run.is_cancelled());
    }

    /// `child_of` does not propagate cancellation to the parent when the
    /// child scope is cancelled.
    #[test]
    fn child_of_does_not_cancel_parent() {
        let parent = CancellationToken::new();
        let run = RunCancellation::child_of(&parent);
        assert!(!parent.is_cancelled());

        run.cancel();
        // The parent should remain un-cancelled.
        assert!(!parent.is_cancelled());
        // The child scope itself is cancelled.
        assert!(run.is_cancelled());
    }
}

//!
//! This module defines [`AgentSnapshot`] and [`SessionSnapshot`] — lightweight
//! value types that capture a point-in-time view of the runtime's live state.
//! They are constructed on-demand from [`Agent`] (harness-core) and
//! [`SessionRuntime`] objects, **not** deserialized from storage.
//!
//! # Intended use
//!
//! ```rust,ignore
//! // From an AgentRunner (or any &Agent reference):
//! let agent_snapshot = AgentSnapshot::from_agent(runner.agent());
//!
//! // From a SessionRuntime:
//! let session_snapshot = runtime.snapshot();  // basic session info
//! ```
//!
//! The snapshot types are the return value of
//! [`SessionClient::snapshot`](crate::handles::SessionClient) and are consumed
//! by frontends (IDE, TUI, WebSocket) to display current session and agent
//! status without acquiring locks on the live runtime objects.

use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, SessionId, Timestamp};

};

use crate::runtime::{SessionStatus, SessionRuntime};

// AgentSnapshot
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A point-in-time projection of a live agent's state (spec §45).
///
/// Constructed via [`AgentSnapshot::from_agent`] which reads the agent's
/// current [`AgentState`](harness_core::agent_state::AgentState) — status,
/// current operation, usage ledger — as well as its immutable identity fields
/// (id, parent_id, backend descriptor).
///
/// Nothing in this struct is persisted; it is a throwaway read used for
/// frontend display, debugging, and inspection.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AgentSnapshot {
    /// The unique identifier of this agent.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// The parent agent's identifier, if any. Root agents have `None`.
    pub parent_id: Option<AgentId>,

    /// The agent's current lifecycle status (Idle, WaitingForBackend,
    /// Executing, Completed, etc.).
    pub status: AgentStatus,
    /// What the agent is currently doing, if anything (backend request,
    /// tool execution, waiting for children, etc.).
    pub current_operation: Option<AgentOperation>,

    /// The backend descriptor this agent is bound to (integration identity
    /// and capability flags).
    pub backend: BackendDescriptor,
    /// A snapshot of the agent's usage metrics at this instant.
    pub usage: AgentUsageSnapshot,
}

impl AgentSnapshot {
    /// Construct an [`AgentSnapshot`] by reading live state from an [`Agent`].
    ///
    /// The agent's id, parent id, status, current operation, backend
    /// descriptor, and usage are all read directly from the agent's in-memory
    /// state — no I/O is performed, and no locks are held.
    ///
    /// # Usage metrics
    ///
    /// The [`AgentUsageMetrics`] are aggregated from the agent's usage ledger
    /// records at the time of the call.  Specifically:
    ///
    /// * `total_runs` — the number of [`UsageRecord`]s in the ledger.
    /// * `total_requests` — the number of records (each record typically
    ///   represents one backend request).
    /// * `total_tool_calls` — the number of records that include a tool_usage.
    /// * `total_tokens` — the sum of `(input_tokens + output_tokens)` across
    ///   all records, or `Unknown` if no records exist.
    /// * `total_cost` — the sum of `cost.amount_usd` across all records, or
    ///   `None` if no records have a cost.
    pub fn from_agent(agent: &Agent) -> Self {
        let mut total_requests = 0u64;
        let mut total_tool_calls = 0u64;
        let mut total_input_tokens = 0u64;
        let mut total_output_tokens = 0u64;
        let mut total_cost: Option<rust_decimal::Decimal> = None;

        for record in &agent.usage.records {
            total_requests += 1;

            if record.tool_usage.is_some() {
                total_tool_calls += 1;
            }

            if let Some(t) = record.model_usage.input_tokens.value() {
                total_input_tokens = total_input_tokens.saturating_add(t);
            }
            if let Some(t) = record.model_usage.output_tokens.value() {
                total_output_tokens = total_output_tokens.saturating_add(t);
            }

            if let Some(ref amount) = record.cost.amount_usd {
                total_cost = Some(total_cost.unwrap_or_default() + amount);
            }
        }

        let total_tokens = if total_requests == 0 {
            UsageValue::new(None)
        } else {
            UsageValue::new(Some(total_input_tokens + total_output_tokens))
        };

        let timestamp = Timestamp::now();
        let timestamp_str = timestamp.as_datetime().to_rfc3339();

        Self {
            id: agent.id,
            parent_id: agent.parent_id,
            status: agent.state.status,
            current_operation: agent.state.current_operation.clone(),
            backend: agent.backend.descriptor.clone(),
            usage: AgentUsageSnapshot {
                agent_id: agent.id.to_string(),
                metrics: AgentUsageMetrics {
                    total_runs: agent.usage.records.len() as u64,
                    total_requests,
                    total_tool_calls,
                    total_tokens,
                    total_cost,
                },
                timestamp: timestamp_str,
            },
        }
    }
}

//! Session client API — the primary frontend-facing handle for interacting
//! with a live session (spec §48, §76).
//!
//! This module defines the [`SessionClient`] trait and its primary
//! implementation, [`SessionApi`], which wraps an [`SessionRuntime`] and
//! provides a clean async interface for sending commands, taking
//! snapshots, and subscribing to events.
//!
//! # Architecture (spec §48)
//!
//! ```text
//! Frontend (IDE, TUI, WebSocket)
//!   │
//!   │  SessionClient trait
//!   │    ├── send(SessionCommand)     → drives session lifecycle
//!   │    ├── snapshot()               → T17 projection of live state
//!   │    └── subscribe()              → SessionEvent stream
//!   │
//!   ▼
//! SessionApi (concrete impl)
//!   │
//!   ├── SessionRuntime (event loop, agent runner, event bus)
//!   └── Arc<SessionRuntime> (shared ownership)
//! ```

use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::sync::broadcast;

use crate::runtime::{SessionCommand, SessionError, SessionEvent, SessionRuntime};
use crate::snapshot::SessionSnapshot;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionEventStream
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A stream of [`SessionEvent`]s emitted by a session.
///
/// This is a [`tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver`] that yields session-level
/// events including agent events, lifecycle changes, and usage updates.
///
/// Multiple frontend components can independently subscribe to the same
/// session's event bus; each gets its own [`SessionEventStream`] with a
/// buffer that starts at the subscription moment (no replay of past events).
pub type SessionEventStream = broadcast::Receiver<SessionEvent>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionClient trait  (spec §48)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The primary API for interacting with a live session.
///
/// Implementations wrap a [`SessionRuntime`] and provide a clean,
/// frontend-friendly interface for:
///
/// * Sending commands ([`send`](Self::send)) — prompts, cancellations,
///   pause/resume, and permission decisions.
/// * Taking point-in-time snapshots ([`snapshot`](Self::snapshot)) of the
///   session's current state via the T17 projection.
/// * Subscribing to the session-level event stream
///   ([`subscribe`](Self::subscribe)) for reactive UI updates.
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// use harness_runtime::handles::{SessionClient, SessionApi};
///
/// let api = SessionApi::new(runtime_arc);
///
/// // Send a prompt to start a run
/// api.send(SessionCommand::Prompt(input)).await?;
///
/// // Inspect live state
/// let snap = api.snapshot().await?;
/// println!("Session status: {:?}", snap.status);
///
/// // Subscribe for events
/// let mut stream = api.subscribe();
/// while let Ok(event) = stream.recv().await {
///     // handle event
/// }
/// ```
pub trait SessionClient {
    /// Send a [`SessionCommand`] to the session's run loop.
    ///
    /// Returns `Ok(())` if the command was accepted, or a [`SessionError`]
    /// if the session has already shut down (the receiver was dropped).
    async fn send(
        &self,
        command: SessionCommand,
    ) -> Result<(), SessionError>;

    /// Return a point-in-time [`SessionSnapshot`] of the session's live
    /// state (spec §45).
    ///
    /// The snapshot includes session identity, lifecycle status, aggregated
    /// usage, and agent snapshots for all active agents.  It is a pure
    /// in-memory read — no I/O or locks are involved.
    ///
    /// This is the T17 projection referenced in the architecture:
    /// a throwaway read used for display, debugging, and inspection.
    async fn snapshot(
        &self,
    ) -> Result<SessionSnapshot, SessionError>;

    /// Subscribe to the session-level event stream.
    ///
    /// Returns a [`SessionEventStream`] (a
    /// [`broadcast::Receiver<SessionEvent>`]) that yields all session
    /// events — agent events (with monotonically increasing
    /// `session_sequence` values), lifecycle changes (`StatusChanged`,
    /// `Completed`, `Failed`), and usage updates.
    ///
    /// Each call creates an independent subscriber starting at the current
    /// broadcast buffer head.  Late subscribers will miss earlier events.
    fn subscribe(&self) -> SessionEventStream;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionApi  (spec §76)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A concrete [`SessionClient`] implementation that wraps an
/// [`Arc<SessionRuntime>`].
///
/// `SessionApi` is the standard frontend-facing handle for a live session.
/// It is cheaply cloneable (the `Arc` is shared) and provides the full
/// [`SessionClient`] API.
///
/// # Construction
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// use std::sync::Arc;
/// use harness_runtime::handles::SessionApi;
/// use harness_runtime::runtime::SessionRuntime;
///
/// let runtime = SessionRuntime::new(/* ... */);
/// let api = SessionApi::new(Arc::new(runtime));
/// ```
///
/// # Thread safety
///
/// `SessionApi` is `Send + Sync` because all mutable state is inside the
/// `SessionRuntime` which uses internal synchronization (MPSC channels,
/// atomics, broadcast).  Multiple tasks can hold clones of the same
/// `SessionApi` and interact with the session concurrently.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SessionApi {
    /// The shared session runtime that backs all operations.
    runtime: Arc<SessionRuntime>,
}

impl SessionApi {
    /// Create a new [`SessionApi`] from an [`Arc<SessionRuntime>`].
    ///
    /// This is the standard construction path.  The `Arc` allows the handle
    /// to be cheaply cloned and shared across tasks.
    pub fn new(runtime: Arc<SessionRuntime>) -> Self {
        Self { runtime }
    }

    /// Returns a reference to the inner [`SessionRuntime`].
    ///
    /// This can be used to access runtime internals (e.g., for testing or
    /// advanced configuration) without going through the `SessionClient`
    /// trait.
    pub fn runtime(&self) -> &SessionRuntime {
        &self.runtime
    }
}

impl SessionClient for SessionApi {
    /// Send a command to the session's run loop.
    ///
    /// Delegates to [`SessionRuntime::send_command`], converting the MPSC
    /// [`SendError`](tokio::sync::mpsc::error::SendError) into a
    /// [`SessionError`] with code `"SESSION_SHUTDOWN"`.
    async fn send(
        &self,
        command: SessionCommand,
    ) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
        self.runtime
            .send_command(command)
            .await
            .map_err(|_| SessionError {
                message: "session run loop has shut down".into(),
                code: "SESSION_SHUTDOWN".into(),
            })
    }

    /// Return a point-in-time [`SessionSnapshot`] via the T17 projection.
    ///
    /// Delegates to [`SessionRuntime::snapshot`] which is a pure in-memory
    /// read.  This method always returns `Ok` — the snapshot is constructed
    /// from live state without I/O.
    async fn snapshot(
        &self,
    ) -> Result<SessionSnapshot, SessionError> {
        Ok(self.runtime.snapshot())
    }

    /// Subscribe to the session-level event stream.
    ///
    /// Delegates to [`SessionEventBus::subscribe`] on the runtime's event
    /// bus.  Each call returns an independent receiver.
    fn subscribe(&self) -> SessionEventStream {
        self.runtime.event_bus.subscribe()
    }
}

//! Session runtime — event bus, session state, and lifecycle.
//!
//! This module provides [`SessionEventBus`], the central aggregation point
//! that transforms per-agent [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s into a session-scoped
//! [`SessionEvent`] stream with monotonically increasing
//! [`session_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::session_sequence) values.
//!
//! It also provides [`SessionRuntime`] — the top-level executor that owns
//! a session's root agent runner, routes [`SessionCommand`]s to the agent,
//! and forwards agent events into the session stream (spec §6.2).
//!
//! ## Architecture (spec §40/§44)
//!
//! ```text
//! Agent
//!   ↓  AgentEventEnvelope (session_sequence: None)
//! SessionEventBus
//!   ├── assigns session_sequence
//!   ├── wraps in SessionEvent::Agent { event }
//!   └── broadcasts to subscribers
//!         ├── IDE
//!         ├── TUI
//!         ├── WebSocket
//!         ├── logging
//!         └── telemetry
//! ```
//!
//! ## SessionRuntime (spec §6.2)
//!
//! ```text
//! External caller
//!   │  SessionCommand::Prompt
//!   ▼
//! SessionRuntime
//!   ├── routes to AgentCommand::StartRun
//!   ├── spawns root AgentRunner (background task)
//!   ├── forwards agent events → SessionEventBus
//!   └── publishes SessionStarted / Completed lifecycle events
//! ```

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicU8, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_core::capabilities::AgentCapabilities;
use harness_protocol::backend::{BackendBinding, BackendReference};
use harness_protocol::commands::{AgentCommand, UserInput};
use harness_protocol::events::{AgentEvent, AgentEventEnvelope};
use harness_protocol::ids::{
    AgentId, ConfigurationId, IntegrationId, PermissionId, RunId, SessionId,
};
use harness_protocol::usage::{AgentBudget, SessionUsageSnapshot};

use crate::agent_runner::{AgentRunner, AgentTask};
use crate::traits::{ExecutionBackend, ToolRegistry, Workspace};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionStatus
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The lifecycle status of a session.
///
/// Mirrors the session state machine transitions defined in spec §44.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum SessionStatus {
    /// The session has been created but has not yet started processing.
    Starting,
    /// The session is actively processing (accepting prompts, running agents).
    Running,
    /// The session has been paused (agents are suspended).
    Paused,
    /// The session completed normally.
    Completed,
    /// The session terminated with an unrecoverable error.
    Failed,
    /// The session was cancelled before completion.
    Cancelled,
}

impl SessionStatus {
    /// Convert this status to a `u8` discriminant for atomic storage.
    pub(crate) fn to_u8(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            SessionStatus::Starting => 0,
            SessionStatus::Running => 1,
            SessionStatus::Paused => 2,
            SessionStatus::Completed => 3,
            SessionStatus::Failed => 4,
            SessionStatus::Cancelled => 5,
        }
    }

    /// Reconstruct a status from a `u8` discriminant.
    ///
    /// Values outside the known range are silently mapped to [`Running`](SessionStatus::Running).
    pub(crate) fn from_u8(val: u8) -> Self {
        match val {
            0 => SessionStatus::Starting,
            1 => SessionStatus::Running,
            2 => SessionStatus::Paused,
            3 => SessionStatus::Completed,
            4 => SessionStatus::Failed,
            5 => SessionStatus::Cancelled,
            _ => SessionStatus::Running,
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionError
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A structured error representing a session-level failure.
///
/// This is distinct from agent-level or backend-level errors — it indicates
/// that the session itself (rather than an individual agent within it) has
/// encountered an unrecoverable condition.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SessionError {
    /// A human-readable description of what went wrong.
    pub message: String,
    /// A machine-readable error code (e.g. `"SESSION_CRASHED"`, `"TIMEOUT"`).
    pub code: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentDescriptor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A lightweight description of an agent within a session.
///
/// Used in [`SessionEvent::AgentAdded`] to notify consumers when a new agent
/// (root or child) is registered.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AgentDescriptor {
    /// The unique identifier of the agent.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// The parent agent's identifier, if any. Root agents have `None`.
    pub parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    /// A human-readable name or label for the agent (e.g. `"root"`, `"research"`).
    pub name: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionEvent
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Events emitted by a session, aggregated from all agents within that session.
///
/// The session is the preferred frontend subscription boundary (spec §44).
/// A frontend subscribes to one session and automatically receives events
/// for the root agent and all descendants through the [`Agent`](Self::Agent)
/// variant.
///
/// Every [`AgentEventEnvelope`] that passes through the session bus receives
/// a monotonically increasing [`session_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::session_sequence)
/// so that consumers can reconstruct a total order across all agents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SessionEvent {
    /// The session has started and is ready to accept commands.
    SessionStarted,

    /// The session's [`SessionStatus`] changed.
    StatusChanged {
        /// The new status of the session.
        status: SessionStatus,
    },

    /// An event originating from one of the session's agents.
    ///
    /// The embedded [`AgentEventEnvelope`] carries all routing metadata
    /// (`session_id`, `agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`, `run_id`) as well as
    /// the per-agent and per-session sequence numbers.
    Agent {
        /// The fully qualified agent event with session-level sequencing.
        event: AgentEventEnvelope,
    },

    /// A new agent was added to the session (root or child).
    AgentAdded {
        /// A descriptor of the newly added agent.
        agent: AgentDescriptor,
    },

    /// An agent was removed from the session (e.g. after completion or failure).
    AgentRemoved {
        /// The identifier of the agent that was removed.
        agent_id: AgentId,
    },

    /// Session-level usage metrics were updated.
    UsageUpdated {
        /// A snapshot of the session's aggregated usage.
        usage: SessionUsageSnapshot,
    },

    /// The session completed successfully.
    Completed,

    /// The session failed with an unrecoverable error.
    Failed {
        /// Details about the failure.
        error: SessionError,
    },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionEventBus
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Aggregates one or more [`AgentRunner`] broadcast channels into a single
/// [`SessionEvent`] stream, assigning monotonically increasing
/// `session_sequence` values to every [`AgentEventEnvelope`] that passes
/// through (spec §40/§44).
///
/// # How it works
///
/// The bus maintains an atomic 64-bit counter that is incremented for each
/// agent event forwarded.  It does **not** own the agent-runner subscriptions
/// directly — callers (typically the [`SessionRuntime`] event loop) invoke
/// [`forward_agent_event`](Self::forward_agent_event) whenever they receive
/// an envelope from an agent runner's broadcast channel, or use the
/// convenience [`spawn_agent_forwarder`](Self::spawn_agent_forwarder) method
/// to hand that responsibility off to a background task.
///
/// # Thread safety
///
/// All methods take `&self` because the sequence counter is an `AtomicU64`.
/// This allows the bus to be shared across multiple forwarding tasks or used
/// from a single event loop without a mutex.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(256);
/// let mut rx = bus.subscribe();
///
/// // Forward an agent event (synchronous)
/// bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);
///
/// // Or spawn a background forwarder for an agent runner's broadcast
/// let arc_bus = Arc::new(bus);
/// SessionEventBus::spawn_agent_forwarder(&arc_bus, agent_runner_receiver);
/// ```
pub struct SessionEventBus {
    /// The output channel — subscribers receive [`SessionEvent`]s.
    output: broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent>,
    /// Monotonic counter incremented for every agent event forwarded.
    /// Atomic so that `forward_agent_event` can be called concurrently
    /// from multiple spawned forwarding tasks.
    session_sequence: AtomicU64,
}

impl SessionEventBus {
    /// Create a new `SessionEventBus` that publishes to the given sender.
    ///
    /// The caller provides the [`broadcast::Sender`] so that multiple
    /// components can share the same underlying channel if needed.
    /// Use [`with_capacity`](Self::with_capacity) for a simpler standalone
    /// creation pattern.
    pub fn new(output: broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent>) -> Self {
        Self {
            output,
            session_sequence: AtomicU64::new(0),
        }
    }

    /// Create a `SessionEventBus` with a freshly allocated broadcast channel
    /// of the given capacity.
    ///
    /// This is the simplest construction — the bus owns the only sender, and
    /// callers subscribe via [`subscribe`](Self::subscribe).
    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let (tx, _) = broadcast::channel(capacity);
        Self::new(tx)
    }

    /// Subscribe to the session-level event stream.
    ///
    /// Returns a [`broadcast::Receiver`] that will receive every
    /// [`SessionEvent`] published on this bus, starting from the most recent
    /// messages still in the buffer (or none if the buffer has already been
    /// exhausted).
    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<SessionEvent> {
        self.output.subscribe()
    }

    /// Return a clone of the inner sender, allowing external code to
    /// publish events directly (e.g. for testing or for forwarding from
    /// other sources).
    pub fn sender(&self) -> broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent> {
        self.output.clone()
    }

    /// Forward an [`AgentEventEnvelope`] from an agent runner into the
    /// session stream.
    ///
    /// This method:
    /// 1. Assigns the next `session_sequence` value to the envelope.
    /// 2. Wraps it in [`SessionEvent::Agent`].
    /// 3. Publishes it on the output broadcast channel.
    ///
    /// If there are no active subscribers, the event is silently dropped
    /// (this is intentional — the bus does not buffer for absent consumers).
    pub fn forward_agent_event(&self, mut envelope: AgentEventEnvelope) {
        let seq = self.session_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        envelope.session_sequence = Some(seq);
        let _ = self.output.send(SessionEvent::Agent { event: envelope });
    }

    /// Publish a lifecycle [`SessionEvent`] that does not originate from a
    /// specific agent (e.g. [`SessionStarted`](SessionEvent::SessionStarted),
    /// [`Completed`](SessionEvent::Completed)).
    ///
    /// Note: this method does **not** assign a `session_sequence` because
    /// non-agent events are not sequenced at the agent-envelope level.
    /// They are delivered in publication order relative to agent events due
    /// to the sequential nature of the broadcast channel.
    ///
    /// If there are no active subscribers, the event is silently dropped.
    pub fn publish(&self, event: SessionEvent) {
        let _ = self.output.send(event);
    }

    /// Spawn a background task that forwards all events from a single
    /// agent runner's [`broadcast::Receiver`] into this session bus.
    ///
    /// The caller provides a reference-counted bus so the spawned task can
    /// hold its own reference.  The returned [`tokio::task::JoinHandle`] can
    /// be used to monitor or cancel the forwarding task.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The forwarding task runs until the agent runner's broadcast sender
    /// is dropped (which causes `recv()` to return `Err(Closed)`) or until
    /// the task is cancelled.  If the receiver lags behind, the task silently
    /// drops the missed events and continues.
    ///
    /// # Example
    ///
    /// ```rust,ignore
    /// let bus = Arc::new(SessionEventBus::with_capacity(256));
    /// let handle = SessionEventBus::spawn_agent_forwarder(&bus, agent_receiver);
    /// ```
    pub fn spawn_agent_forwarder(
        bus: &Arc<Self>,
        agent_receiver: broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    ) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> {
        let bus = Arc::clone(bus);
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            loop {
                match agent_receiver.recv().await {
                    Ok(envelope) => {
                        bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);
                    }
                    Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => {
                        // The agent runner shut down; no more events.
                        break;
                    }
                    Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => {
                        // We missed some events.  Best-effort forwarder —
                        // continue with the next available event.
                        continue;
                    }
                }
            }
        })
    }
}

/// The live session runtime, owning the root agent runner and event bus.
///
/// `SessionRuntime` ties together the session's state, its injected backend
/// and workspace, and the event aggregation bus.  On construction it:
///
/// 1. Creates the root [`Agent`] and wraps it in an [`AgentRunner`].
/// 2. Spawns the agent runner on a background tokio task.
/// 3. Spawns a run-loop task that:
///    - Publishes [`SessionEvent::SessionStarted`].
///    - Receives [`SessionCommand`]s and routes [`Prompt`](SessionCommand::Prompt)
///      to [`AgentCommand::StartRun`].
///    - Forwards agent events through [`SessionEventBus::forward_agent_event`].
///    - Publishes [`SessionEvent::Completed`] when the agent completes.
///
/// # Architecture
///
/// ```text
///           SessionCommand::Prompt
///                    │
///                    ▼
///        SessionRuntime run-loop
///                    │
///         ┌──────────┼──────────────┐
///         ▼          ▼              ▼
///   AgentCommand  AgentEvent    SessionEvent::Completed
///   ::StartRun    → forwarded    (terminal)
///         │
///         ▼
///   AgentRunner (bg task)
///         │
///         ├── FakeBackend (test) / real backend
///         └── events broadcast
/// ```
pub struct SessionRuntime {
    /// The durable session identity and metadata.
    pub state: SessionState,

    /// The execution backend injected for this session.
    pub default_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,

    /// The workspace injected for this session.
    pub workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,

    /// The event bus that aggregates agent events into the session stream.
    pub event_bus: SessionEventBus,

    /// Tracks the current lifecycle status of the session.
    ///
    /// Initialised to [`Running`](SessionStatus::Running) on construction.
    /// The run-loop task updates this to [`Completed`](SessionStatus::Completed),
    /// [`Failed`](SessionStatus::Failed), or [`Cancelled`](SessionStatus::Cancelled)
    /// when the session terminates.
    ///
    /// Read by [`snapshot`](Self::snapshot) to return the current status.
    pub status: Arc<AtomicU8>,

    /// Sender for [`SessionCommand`]s — the run loop receives on the
    /// corresponding receiver.
    command_tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<SessionCommand>,
}

impl SessionRuntime {
    /// Create a new `SessionRuntime` and start its background run loop.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    ///
    /// * `state` — the session's durable identity.
    /// * `default_backend` — the backend all agent runs in this session
    ///   will use.
    /// * `workspace` — the workspace injected for file I/O.
    /// * `event_bus` — the bus onto which session events are published.
    /// * `system_prompt` — the system instructions for the root agent.
    /// * `capabilities` — the capabilities granted to the root agent.
    /// * `tool_registry` — the runtime-wide tool registry.
    /// * `budget` — the budget constraints for the root agent.
    pub fn new(
        state: SessionState,
        default_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
        workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
        event_bus: SessionEventBus,
        system_prompt: String,
        capabilities: AgentCapabilities,
        tool_registry: ToolRegistry,
        budget: AgentBudget,
    ) -> Self {
        // ── Command channels ──────────────────────────────────────────
        let (command_tx, command_rx) =
            tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<SessionCommand>(32);
        let (agent_cmd_tx, agent_cmd_rx) =
            tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<AgentCommand>(32);
        let (agent_evt_tx, agent_evt_rx) =
            tokio::sync::broadcast::channel::<AgentEventEnvelope>(256);

        // ── Root agent ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        let agent = Agent::new(
            state.root_agent_id,
            state.id,
            None, // root agent has no parent
            system_prompt,
            BackendBinding {
                reference: BackendReference {
                    integration: IntegrationId::new(),
                    configuration: ConfigurationId::new(),
                    model: None,
                },
                descriptor: default_backend.descriptor(),
            },
            capabilities,
            budget,
        );

        // ── Agent task (mailbox) ──────────────────────────────────────
        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
        let agent_task = AgentTask {
            id: state.root_agent_id,
            commands: agent_cmd_rx,
            events: agent_evt_tx,
            cancel: cancel.clone(),
        };

        let agent_runner = AgentRunner::new(
            agent,
            agent_task,
            default_backend.clone(),
            tool_registry,
            agent_cmd_tx.clone(),
        );

        // Spawn the agent runner on a background task.
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            agent_runner.run().await;
        });

        // ── Session status tracking ──────────────────────────────────
        let status: Arc<AtomicU8> =
            Arc::new(AtomicU8::new(SessionStatus::Running.to_u8()));
        let status_for_loop = Arc::clone(&status);

        // ── Session run loop ──────────────────────────────────────────
        // Wrap the event bus in an Arc so the spawned loop can share it.
        let bus = Arc::new(event_bus);
        Self::spawn_run_loop(
            Arc::clone(&bus),
            command_rx,
            agent_cmd_tx,
            agent_evt_rx,
            cancel,
            status_for_loop,
        );

        // Extract the plain event bus back from the Arc.
        // At this point the Arc has exactly two references: the local
        // `bus` and the one moved into `spawn_run_loop`'s closure.
        // We unwrap the local one and drop it — the spawned task keeps
        // its own clone alive.
        let inner_bus = Arc::try_unwrap(bus)
            .expect("SessionRuntime: event_bus Arc must have exactly one strong ref after spawn");

        Self {
            state,
            default_backend,
            workspace,
            event_bus: inner_bus,
            status,
            command_tx,
        }
    }

    /// Spawn the background run-loop task.
    ///
    /// This task:
    /// 1. Publishes [`SessionEvent::SessionStarted`].
    /// 2. Listens for [`SessionCommand`]s and [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s.
    /// 3. Routes [`SessionCommand::Prompt`] to [`AgentCommand::StartRun`].
    /// 4. Routes [`SessionCommand::CancelRun`]/[`CancelAgent`] to
    ///    [`AgentCommand::Cancel`] (the core translation).
    /// 5. Forwards agent events through the session bus.
    /// 6. Updates the session [`status`](Self::status) to terminal state
    ///    ([`Completed`](SessionStatus::Completed),
    ///    [`Failed`](SessionStatus::Failed), or
    ///    [`Cancelled`](SessionStatus::Cancelled)).
    /// 7. Publishes [`SessionEvent::Completed`] / [`Failed`](SessionEvent::Failed).
    fn spawn_run_loop(
        bus: Arc<SessionEventBus>,
        mut command_rx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<SessionCommand>,
        agent_cmd_tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>,
        mut agent_evt_rx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope>,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
        status: Arc<AtomicU8>,
    ) {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            // Signal that the session is live.
            bus.publish(SessionEvent::SessionStarted);

            loop {
                tokio::select! {
                    // ── Session command received ──────────────────────
                    cmd = command_rx.recv() => {
                        let Some(cmd) = cmd else {
                            // All senders dropped — shut down.
                            status.store(SessionStatus::Failed.to_u8(), Ordering::Release);
                            break;
                        };

                        match cmd {
                            SessionCommand::Prompt(input) => {
                                // Route Prompt → StartRun.
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::StartRun { input })
                                    .await;
                            }
                            SessionCommand::CancelRun { .. } => {
                                // Translate CancelRun → AgentCommand::Cancel
                                // for an orderly state-machine transition.
                                // The token cancellation additionally aborts
                                // any in-flight backend/tool calls.
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::Cancel)
                                    .await;
                                cancel.cancel();
                            }
                            SessionCommand::CancelAgent { .. } => {
                                // Translate CancelAgent → AgentCommand::Cancel.
                                // In a multi-agent session this would target
                                // the specific agent; for Phase 2 the single
                                // root agent receives the Cancel command.
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::Cancel)
                                    .await;
                                cancel.cancel();
                            }
                            SessionCommand::PauseAgent { .. } => {
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::Pause)
                                    .await;
                            }
                            SessionCommand::ResumeAgent { .. } => {
                                let _ = agent_cmd_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::Resume)
                                    .await;
                            }
                            // Permission routing is deferred to a later phase.
                            SessionCommand::ApprovePermission { .. }
                            | SessionCommand::RejectPermission { .. } => {}
                        }
                    }

                    // ── Agent event received ──────────────────────────
                    agent_result = agent_evt_rx.recv() => {
                        match agent_result {
                            Ok(envelope) => {
                                // Check for terminal agent events *before*
                                // forwarding so we can also emit the
                                // session-level terminal event.
                                let is_completed = matches!(
                                    envelope.event,
                                    AgentEvent::Completed { .. }
                                );
                                let is_failed = matches!(
                                    envelope.event,
                                    AgentEvent::Failed { .. }
                                );

                                // Assign session_sequence and publish.
                                bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);

                                // Publish session-level terminal event.
                                if is_completed {
                                    status.store(SessionStatus::Completed.to_u8(), Ordering::Release);
                                    bus.publish(SessionEvent::Completed);
                                    break;
                                }
                                if is_failed {
                                    status.store(SessionStatus::Failed.to_u8(), Ordering::Release);
                                    bus.publish(SessionEvent::Failed {
                                        error: SessionError {
                                            message: "Agent run failed".into(),
                                            code: "AGENT_FAILED".into(),
                                        },
                                    });
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                            Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => {
                                // Agent runner shut down — no more events.
                                status.store(SessionStatus::Failed.to_u8(), Ordering::Release);
                                break;
                            }
                            Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => {
                                // We missed some events — best-effort
                                // continue with the next one.
                                continue;
                            }
                        }
                    }

                    // ── Cancellation requested ────────────────────────
                    _ = cancel.cancelled() => {
                        status.store(SessionStatus::Cancelled.to_u8(), Ordering::Release);
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }

    /// Returns a clone of the command sender, allowing external code to
    /// send [`SessionCommand`]s to this session.
    pub fn command_tx(&self) -> tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<SessionCommand> {
        self.command_tx.clone()
    }

    /// Send a [`SessionCommand`] to the session's run loop.
    ///
    /// Returns an error if the run loop has already shut down (the receiver
    /// was dropped).
    pub async fn send_command(
        &self,
        command: SessionCommand,
    ) -> Result<(), tokio::sync::mpsc::error::SendError<SessionCommand>> {
        self.command_tx.send(command).await
    }
}

    /// Returns a minimal [`AgentEventEnvelope`] for testing.
    fn sample_envelope() -> AgentEventEnvelope {
        AgentEventEnvelope {
            event_id: EventId::new(),
            session_id: harness_protocol::ids::SessionId::new(),
            agent_id: harness_protocol::ids::AgentId::new(),
            parent_agent_id: None,
            run_id: Some(RunId::new()),
            agent_sequence: 0,

    /// Forwarding an agent event assigns a `session_sequence` and wraps it
    /// in [`SessionEvent::Agent`].
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn forward_agent_event_assigns_sequence() {
        let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(16);
        let mut rx = bus.subscribe();

        let envelope = sample_envelope();
        assert!(envelope.session_sequence.is_none());

        bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);

        let event = rx.recv().await.expect("should receive session event");
        match event {
            SessionEvent::Agent { event } => {
                assert_eq!(
                    event.session_sequence,
                    Some(0),
                    "first forwarded event gets session_sequence = 0"
                );
            }
            other => panic!("expected SessionEvent::Agent, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    /// The `session_sequence` counter increments monotonically across
    /// multiple forwarded events.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn session_sequence_is_monotonic() {
        let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(16);
        let mut rx = bus.subscribe();

        bus.forward_agent_event(sample_envelope());
        bus.forward_agent_event(sample_envelope());
        bus.forward_agent_event(sample_envelope());

        let mut sequences = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            let event = rx.recv().await.expect("should receive");
            if let SessionEvent::Agent { event } = event {
                sequences.push(event.session_sequence);
            }
        }

        assert_eq!(sequences, vec![Some(0), Some(1), Some(2)]);
    }

    /// Publishing a lifecycle event does not consume a `session_sequence`
    /// (the sequence is only assigned to agent envelopes).
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn publish_lifecycle_event() {
        let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(16);
        let mut rx = bus.subscribe();

        bus.publish(SessionEvent::SessionStarted);
        bus.publish(SessionEvent::Completed);

        let first = rx.recv().await.expect("SessionStarted");
        assert!(
            matches!(first, SessionEvent::SessionStarted),
            "expected SessionStarted"
        );

        let second = rx.recv().await.expect("Completed");
        assert!(
            matches!(second, SessionEvent::Completed),
            "expected Completed"
        );
    }

    /// The sequence counter is not affected by lifecycle events — only
    /// agent events advance it.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn lifecycle_events_do_not_advance_session_sequence() {
        let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(16);
        let mut rx = bus.subscribe();

        bus.publish(SessionEvent::SessionStarted);
        bus.forward_agent_event(sample_envelope());
        bus.publish(SessionEvent::Completed);

        // Consume SessionStarted
        let _ = rx.recv().await;

        // The agent event should have sequence 0 (lifecycle didn't advance it)
        let event = rx.recv().await.expect("agent event");
        match event {
            SessionEvent::Agent { event } => {
                assert_eq!(event.session_sequence, Some(0));
            }
            other => panic!("expected Agent, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    /// Multiple subscribers each receive all events.

    async fn multiple_subscribers() {
        let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(16);

        let mut rx2 = bus.subscribe();

        bus.forward_agent_event(sample_envelope());

        let ev1 = rx1.recv().await;

    /// Forwarding many events in sequence preserves ordering.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn event_ordering() {
        let bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(64);
        let mut rx = bus.subscribe();

        let count = 50;
        for i in 0..count {
            let mut envelope = sample_envelope();
            envelope.agent_sequence = i;
            bus.forward_agent_event(envelope);
        }

        for i in 0..count {
            let event = rx.recv().await.expect("event");
            match event {
                SessionEvent::Agent { event } => {
                    assert_eq!(
                        event.agent_sequence, i,
                        "agent_sequence should match send order"
                    );
                    assert_eq!(
                        event.session_sequence,
                        Some(i),
                        "session_sequence should match send order"
                    );
                }
                _ => panic!("expected Agent event"),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Subscribing to the session event bus and sending
    /// [`SessionCommand::Prompt`] produces a well-ordered [`SessionEvent`]
    /// stream including [`SessionStarted`](SessionEvent::SessionStarted),
    /// wrapped [`Agent`](SessionEvent::Agent) events, and
    /// [`Completed`](SessionEvent::Completed).
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn session_runtime_prompt_produces_ordered_events() {
        use harness_protocol::usage::{Cost, ModelUsage};

        let request_id = RequestId::new();

        // Script a FakeBackend that emits a text delta and then completes.
        let scripted_events = vec![
            ExecutionEvent::TextDelta {
                request_id,
                delta: "Hello from session runtime! ".into(),
            },
            ExecutionEvent::Completed {
                request_id,
                result: ExecutionResult {
                    request_id,
                    usage: ModelUsage::default(),
                    cost: Cost::default(),
                    finish_reason: "end_turn".into(),
                },
            },
        ];

        let backend = Arc::new(FakeBackend::new(
            scripted_events,
            Ok(ExecutionResult {
                request_id,
                usage: ModelUsage::default(),
                cost: Cost::default(),
                finish_reason: "end_turn".into(),
            }),
        ));

        let workspace = Arc::new(FakeWorkspace::new());
        let event_bus = SessionEventBus::with_capacity(64);
        let mut session_rx = event_bus.subscribe();

        let session_id = SessionId::new();
        let root_agent_id = AgentId::new();

        let state = SessionState {
            id: session_id,
            root_agent_id,
            metadata: SessionMetadata {
                title: "test session".into(),
            },
        };

        let capabilities = AgentCapabilities {
            tools: AgentToolset {
                tools: HashMap::new(),
            },
            can_spawn_agents: false,
            max_child_depth: None,
            workspace: WorkspaceCapabilities {
                can_read: false,
                can_write: false,
                can_search: false,
            },
            backend: BackendCapabilities::default(),
        };

        let _runtime = SessionRuntime::new(
            state,
            backend,
            workspace,
            event_bus,
            "You are a helpful assistant.".into(),
            capabilities,
            ToolRegistry::new(),
            AgentBudget::default(),
        );

        // Send a prompt to start a run.
        _runtime
            .send_command(SessionCommand::Prompt(UserInput {
                text: "hello from test".into(),
                attachments: vec![],
            }))
            .await
            .expect("send Prompt");

        // Collect all session events until we see Completed or time out.
        let mut events: Vec<SessionEvent> = Vec::new();

        loop {
            let result = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), session_rx.recv()).await;

            match result {
                Ok(Ok(event)) => {
                    let is_done =
                        matches!(event, SessionEvent::Completed)
                        || matches!(event, SessionEvent::Failed { .. });
                    events.push(event);
                    if is_done {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                Ok(Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed)) => break,
                Ok(Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_))) => continue,
                Err(_elapsed) => {
                    panic!(
                        "timed out waiting for Completed event; collected {} events so far",
                        events.len()
                    );
                }
            }
        }

        // ---- Assertions ----

        // We must have received at least the lifecycle events.
        assert!(
            events.len() >= 2,
            "expected at least 2 events (SessionStarted + Completed), got {}",
            events.len()
        );

        // The first event must be SessionStarted.
        assert!(
            matches!(events[0], SessionEvent::SessionStarted),
            "first event should be SessionStarted, got {:?}",
            events[0]
        );

        // The last event must be Completed.
        assert!(
            matches!(events.last().unwrap(), SessionEvent::Completed),
            "last event should be Completed, got {:?}",
            events.last()
        );

        // There should be at least one Agent event (RunStarted and possibly
        // TextDelta from the FakeBackend).
        let agent_events: Vec<&SessionEvent> = events
            .iter()
            .filter(|e| matches!(e, SessionEvent::Agent { .. }))
            .collect();

        assert!(
            !agent_events.is_empty(),
            "expected at least one Agent event in the stream"
        );

        // Every Agent event must have a session_sequence assigned.
        for evt in &agent_events {
            if let SessionEvent::Agent { event } = evt {
                assert!(
                    event.session_sequence.is_some(),
                    "each Agent event must have a session_sequence assigned"
                );
            }
        }

        // The final event before Completed should be a terminal agent event
        // (or Completed itself if there are trailing lifecycle events).
        // At minimum, verify that SessionStarted precedes every Agent event,
        // and Completed is last.

        let first_agent_idx = events
            .iter()
            .position(|e| matches!(e, SessionEvent::Agent { .. }));
        let completed_idx = events
            .iter()
            .rposition(|e| matches!(e, SessionEvent::Completed));

        if let Some(agent_start) = first_agent_idx {
            assert!(
                0 < agent_start,
                "SessionStarted (index 0) should precede all Agent events"
            );
        }

        if let Some(done) = completed_idx {
            assert_eq!(
                done,
                events.len() - 1,
                "Completed must be the last event in the stream"
            );
        }
    }

                Ok(Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed)) => break,

//! Snapshot projections of live agent and session state (spec §45).
//!
//! This module defines [`AgentSnapshot`] and [`SessionSnapshot`] — lightweight
//! value types that capture a point-in-time view of the runtime's live state.
//! They are constructed on-demand from [`Agent`] (harness-core) and
//! [`SessionRuntime`] objects, **not** deserialized from storage.
//!
//! # Intended use
//!
//! ```rust,ignore
//! // From an AgentRunner (or any &Agent reference):
//! let agent_snapshot = AgentSnapshot::from_agent(runner.agent());
//!
//! // From a SessionRuntime:
//! let session_snapshot = runtime.snapshot();  // basic session info
//! ```
//!
//! The snapshot types are the return value of
//! [`SessionClient::snapshot`](crate::handles::SessionClient) and are consumed
//! by frontends (IDE, TUI, WebSocket) to display current session and agent
//! status without acquiring locks on the live runtime objects.

use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_protocol::backend::BackendDescriptor;
use harness_protocol::commands::{AgentOperation, AgentStatus};
use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, SessionId, Timestamp};
use harness_protocol::usage::{
    AgentUsageMetrics, AgentUsageSnapshot, CumulativeUsage, SessionUsageSnapshot, UsageValue,
};

use crate::runtime::{SessionStatus, SessionRuntime};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentSnapshot
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A point-in-time projection of a live agent's state (spec §45).
///
/// Constructed via [`AgentSnapshot::from_agent`] which reads the agent's
/// current [`AgentState`](harness_core::agent_state::AgentState) — status,
/// current operation, usage ledger — as well as its immutable identity fields
/// (id, parent_id, backend descriptor).
///
/// Nothing in this struct is persisted; it is a throwaway read used for
/// frontend display, debugging, and inspection.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AgentSnapshot {
    /// The unique identifier of this agent.
    pub id: AgentId,
    /// The parent agent's identifier, if any. Root agents have `None`.
    pub parent_id: Option<AgentId>,

    /// The agent's current lifecycle status (Idle, WaitingForBackend,
    /// Executing, Completed, etc.).
    pub status: AgentStatus,
    /// What the agent is currently doing, if anything (backend request,
    /// tool execution, waiting for children, etc.).
    pub current_operation: Option<AgentOperation>,

    /// The backend descriptor this agent is bound to (integration identity
    /// and capability flags).
    pub backend: BackendDescriptor,
    /// A snapshot of the agent's usage metrics at this instant.
    pub usage: AgentUsageSnapshot,
}

impl AgentSnapshot {
    /// Construct an [`AgentSnapshot`] by reading live state from an [`Agent`].
    ///
    /// The agent's id, parent id, status, current operation, backend
    /// descriptor, and usage are all read directly from the agent's in-memory
    /// state — no I/O is performed, and no locks are held.
    ///
    /// # Usage metrics
    ///
    /// The [`AgentUsageMetrics`] are aggregated from the agent's usage ledger
    /// records at the time of the call.  Specifically:
    ///
    /// * `total_runs` — the number of [`UsageRecord`]s in the ledger.
    /// * `total_requests` — the number of records (each record typically
    ///   represents one backend request).
    /// * `total_tool_calls` — the number of records that include a tool_usage.
    /// * `total_tokens` — the sum of `(input_tokens + output_tokens)` across
    ///   all records, or `Unknown` if no records exist.
    /// * `total_cost` — the sum of `cost.amount_usd` across all records, or
    ///   `None` if no records have a cost.
    pub fn from_agent(agent: &Agent) -> Self {
        let mut total_requests = 0u64;
        let mut total_tool_calls = 0u64;
        let mut total_input_tokens = 0u64;
        let mut total_output_tokens = 0u64;
        let mut total_cost: Option<rust_decimal::Decimal> = None;

        for record in &agent.usage.records {
            total_requests += 1;

            if record.tool_usage.is_some() {
                total_tool_calls += 1;
            }

            if let Some(t) = record.model_usage.input_tokens.value() {
                total_input_tokens = total_input_tokens.saturating_add(t);
            }
            if let Some(t) = record.model_usage.output_tokens.value() {
                total_output_tokens = total_output_tokens.saturating_add(t);
            }

            if let Some(ref amount) = record.cost.amount_usd {
                total_cost = Some(total_cost.unwrap_or_default() + amount);
            }
        }

        let total_tokens = if total_requests == 0 {
            UsageValue::new(None)
        } else {
            UsageValue::new(Some(total_input_tokens + total_output_tokens))
        };

        let timestamp = Timestamp::now();
        let timestamp_str = timestamp.as_datetime().to_rfc3339();

        Self {
            id: agent.id,
            parent_id: agent.parent_id,
            status: agent.state.status,
            current_operation: agent.state.current_operation.clone(),
            backend: agent.backend.descriptor.clone(),
            usage: AgentUsageSnapshot {
                agent_id: agent.id.to_string(),
                metrics: AgentUsageMetrics {
                    total_runs: agent.usage.records.len() as u64,
                    total_requests,
                    total_tool_calls,
                    total_tokens,
                    total_cost,
                },
                timestamp: timestamp_str,
            },
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionSnapshot
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A point-in-time projection of a live session's state (spec §45).
///
/// Constructed via [`SessionRuntime::snapshot`] or via the struct's own
/// [`new`](SessionSnapshot::new) constructor when the caller already has
/// the agent snapshot data.
///
/// Like [`AgentSnapshot`], this is a throwaway read — nothing is persisted
/// or cached.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SessionSnapshot {
    /// The globally unique session identifier.
    pub id: SessionId,
    /// The session's lifecycle status (Starting, Running, Completed, etc.).
    pub status: SessionStatus,

    /// The identifier of the root agent in this session.
    pub root_agent_id: AgentId,
    /// Snapshots of all agents currently alive in this session (root +
    /// descendants).
    pub agents: Vec<AgentSnapshot>,

    /// Aggregated usage for the entire session at this instant.
    pub usage: SessionUsageSnapshot,
}

impl SessionSnapshot {
    /// Construct a [`SessionSnapshot`] from its constituent parts.
    ///
    /// This is a pure data constructor — all fields must be provided by the
    /// caller.  The intended production path is [`SessionRuntime::snapshot`],
    /// which populates the session-level fields and accepts agent snapshots.
    pub fn new(
        id: SessionId,
        status: SessionStatus,
        root_agent_id: AgentId,
        agents: Vec<AgentSnapshot>,
        usage: SessionUsageSnapshot,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            status,
            root_agent_id,
            agents,
            usage,
        }
    }

    /// Build a [`SessionSnapshot`] from the session's identity and status,
    /// a list of agent snapshots, and an aggregated usage snapshot.
    ///
    /// This is equivalent to [`new`](Self::new) but makes the code
    /// site slightly more self-documenting.
    pub fn from_parts(
        id: SessionId,
        status: SessionStatus,
        root_agent_id: AgentId,
        agents: Vec<AgentSnapshot>,
        usage: SessionUsageSnapshot,
    ) -> Self {
        Self::new(id, status, root_agent_id, agents, usage)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionRuntime projection
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

impl SessionRuntime {
    /// Return a point-in-time [`SessionSnapshot`] of this session's live state.
    ///
    /// The returned snapshot contains session-level identity, the current
    /// lifecycle status (read from the runtime's atomic tracker), and the
    /// root agent identifier.  Agent snapshots are an empty vector because
    /// [`SessionRuntime`] does not directly hold references to the root
    /// [`Agent`] (it is owned by a background
    /// [`AgentRunner`](crate::agent_runner::AgentRunner) task).
    ///
    /// To obtain a fully populated snapshot, construct agent snapshots via
    /// [`AgentSnapshot::from_agent`] and pass them along with the session
    /// snapshot to [`SessionSnapshot::from_parts`]:
    ///
    /// ```rust,ignore
    /// let session_snap = runtime.snapshot();
    /// let agent_snap = AgentSnapshot::from_agent(agent_runner.agent());
    /// let full = SessionSnapshot::from_parts(
    ///     session_snap.id,
    ///     session_snap.status,
    ///     session_snap.root_agent_id,
    ///     vec![agent_snap],
    ///     session_snap.usage,
    /// );
    /// ```
    ///
    /// For a higher-level API that bundles this logic see
    /// [`SessionClient::snapshot`](crate::handles::SessionClient).
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> SessionSnapshot {
        // Read the current lifecycle status from the atomic tracker that
        // is updated by the run-loop task on terminal transitions.
        let current_status =
            SessionStatus::from_u8(self.status.load(Ordering::Acquire));

        let timestamp = Timestamp::now();
        let timestamp_str = timestamp.as_datetime().to_rfc3339();

        SessionSnapshot {
            id: self.state.id,
            status: current_status,
            root_agent_id: self.state.root_agent_id,
            agents: Vec::new(),
            usage: SessionUsageSnapshot {
                session_id: self.state.id.to_string(),
                cumulative: CumulativeUsage {
                    total_tokens: UsageValue::new(None),
                    total_cost: None,
                    total_requests: 0,
                },
                timestamp: timestamp_str,
            },
        }
    }
}

                reference: BackendReference {
                    integration: IntegrationId::new(),
